<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">
<span id="id1" class="ltx_tabular ltx_align_top">
<span class="ltx_tbody">
<span id="id1.1" class="ltx_tr">
<span id="id1.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">Lama El Halabi</span></span>
<span id="id1.2" class="ltx_tr">
<span id="id1.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">Stanford University</span></span>
<span id="id1.3" class="ltx_tr">
<span id="id1.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="id1.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">lie08@stanford.edu</span></span></span>
</span>
</span>
 

<span id="id2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_align_top">
<span class="ltx_tbody">
<span id="id2.1" class="ltx_tr">
<span id="id2.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">Adam Brandt</span></span>
<span id="id2.2" class="ltx_tr">
<span id="id2.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">Stanford University</span></span>
<span id="id2.3" class="ltx_tr">
<span id="id2.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="id2.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">abrandt@stanford.edu</span></span></span>
</span>
</span>
</span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Adaptive Conformal Inference (ACI) extends conformal prediction to non-exchangeable settings by adjusting the nominal miscoverage level online in response to recent coverage errors. When forecasts are issued with horizon <math id="abstract1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>, however, the outcome needed to evaluate a prediction is observed only <math id="abstract1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> steps later, so these adaptive updates must rely on delayed feedback. We study this setting and ask how the effect of delay depends on the persistence of the residual process. First, we show that the <math id="abstract1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>-delayed ACI recursion can be decomposed into <math id="abstract1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> interleaved ACI-like sequences. This representation yields a finite-sample bound on long-run empirical coverage with explicit dependence on <math id="abstract1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>. We also derive an approximate marginal coverage bound that relates coverage deviation to changes in the underlying environment across the forecast horizon and to the adaptation rate <math id="abstract1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>. We then introduce the delay-to-memory ratio <math id="abstract1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=\tau/L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=\tau/L</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="abstract1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> is the time scale over which the temporal signal driving non-exchangeability decays. Simulation results show that the usefulness of this ratio depends on the form of temporal dependence: it strongly organizes performance under AR(1) dependence, is less predictive of overall performance under GARCH(1,1) and Markov switching, but more clearly characterizes when scale normalization remains useful in those settings. Abrupt mean- and variance-shift experiments further show that the preferred adaptation rate depends on the residual dynamics. Overall, the results show that the effect of forecast delay is best understood relative to the time scale over which past residual information remains relevant.</p>
  
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Conformal prediction provides a principled framework for uncertainty quantification that can be applied to any black-box prediction model <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shafer and Vovk, 2008</a>)</cite>. It converts point predictions into prediction sets with valid coverage guarantees without requiring strong distributional assumptions. Classical conformal methods rely on exchangeability, but recent work has extended conformal prediction to settings with distribution shifts through reweighting <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Barber et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, distributionally robust methods <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cauchois et al., 2021</a>)</cite>, and online learning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gibbs and Candès, 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zaffran et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gibbs and Candès, 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bhatnagar et al., 2023</a>)</cite>. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gibbs and Candès (2021)</a></cite> introduced Adaptive Conformal Inference (ACI), which responds to distribution shifts by updating the miscoverage level online according to whether recently issued prediction sets cover their targets. In its standard form, however, ACI assumes that the outcome needed to evaluate a prediction is available before the next update is made.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Forecasting with a fixed lead time changes this setting. If a prediction issued at time <math id="S1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> targets the outcome at some future time <math id="S1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t+\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t+\tau</annotation></semantics></math>, its coverage outcome is not observed until <math id="S1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> steps later. The adaptive update must therefore operate using delayed feedback. In extreme cases, there may be significant delay before the effectiveness of a coverage shift can be determined. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gibbs and Candès (2021)</a></cite> identify this as an open direction. The importance of this delay depends on the dynamics of the residual process. A delay of ten steps may be substantial for a process whose dependence disappears within a few observations, but relatively short for one whose residual structure persists over much longer horizons. Thus, the relevant question is not simply whether feedback is delayed, but whether the information contained in that feedback remains useful at the forecast target. Understanding <em id="S1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">when</em> delay becomes consequential is the central question of this paper.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<section id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Related work:</h4>

<div id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Recent work on multi-step conformal forecasting also encounters delayed feedback: a forecast issued at time <math id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> for the outcome at time <math id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t+\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t+\tau</annotation></semantics></math> cannot be evaluated until that outcome is observed <math id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> steps later. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Szabadváry (2024)</a></cite> extend ACI to this setting by maintaining a separate adaptive sequence for each forecast horizon, with horizon-specific target miscoverage levels and learning rates. Their construction inherits ACI-style finite-sample coverage-frequency guarantees at each horizon and for the overall error rate. Their numerical examples illustrate these choices on electricity-demand forecasts, but do not systematically study how delayed feedback affects adaptation or how its effect depends on the persistence of the underlying process.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang and Hyndman (2026)</a></cite> introduce Multi-step Adaptive Conformal Prediction (MACP) as a multi-step extension of ACI and use it as a baseline for their proposed Autocorrelated Multi-step Conformal Prediction method (AcMCP). AcMCP explicitly exploits temporal dependence in multi-step forecast errors. They show that optimal <math id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>-step-ahead forecast errors, where <math id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the forecast horizon, follow an approximate moving-average process of order <math id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h-1</annotation></semantics></math>, denoted MA<math id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(h-1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(h-1)</annotation></semantics></math>, under a general non-stationary autoregressive data-generating process. AcMCP uses this structure to predict part of the upcoming forecast error from historical and preceding-horizon errors. This predicted error component is incorporated directly into the conformal quantile update, alongside feedback terms designed to control long-run coverage. Their simulation studies consider forecast horizons of up to three time steps.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">A broader line of work uses temporal or multi-step information to improve online conformal adaptation. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al. (2024)</a></cite> propose Bellman Conformal Inference (BCI), which uses available multi-step prediction intervals within a stochastic-control problem to select the nominal miscoverage level while explicitly trading off coverage and interval length. Rather than updating the ACI level directly, BCI optimizes the current decision using information about predicted future intervals while retaining a long-run coverage guarantee. More recently, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al. (2026)</a></cite> propose Optimization-Based Online Conformal Prediction (O<sup id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_sup">2</sup>CP), a general framework that augments online conformal methods such as ACI and conformal PID with cross-horizon optimization. O<sup id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_sup">2</sup>CP constructs admissible sets around the control variables produced by the underlying online update and then jointly selects values across forecast horizons using an estimated cross-horizon error distribution, preserving the long-run marginal coverage guarantee of the base procedure. These approaches illustrate complementary ways of using temporal information beyond the most recent coverage error: BCI uses multi-step forecasts to improve interval efficiency, while O<sup id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1.3" class="ltx_sup">2</sup>CP exploits dependence across forecast horizons.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Related work also considers missing or intermittent rather than delayed-but-guaranteed feedback <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Skalse et al., 2026</a>)</cite>. Separately, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gibbs and Candès (2024)</a></cite>, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Angelopoulos et al. (2023)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Angelopoulos et al. (2024)</a></cite>, and <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zaffran et al. (2022)</a></cite> extend ACI through step-size adaptation, expert aggregation, and control-theoretic formulations under distribution shift, but do not focus on delayed feedback.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Taken together, these works address several consequences of multi-step prediction and imperfect feedback, including horizon-specific adaptation, dependence among multi-step forecast errors, cross-horizon optimization, and limited feedback. Our focus is complementary: we study the delayed ACI recursion itself and ask how the consequences of a forecast delay depend on the persistence of the temporal signal driving non-exchangeability. Rather than exploiting a particular temporal dependence structure to improve interval construction, we use persistence as an explanatory time scale and examine when feedback remains informative relative to the delay.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Contributions:</h4>

<div id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This paper makes two main contributions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ol id="S1.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">A delay-to-memory diagnostic for adaptive conformal inference with delayed feedback:</span>
We characterize the feedback delay relative to the persistence of the temporal signal driving non-exchangeability through the ratio
<math id="S1.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=\tau/L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=\tau/L</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S1.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the time scale over which that signal decays. For each persistent residual process, <math id="S1.I1.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> is defined from the decay rate of the relevant dependence structure: residual autocorrelation for AR(1), dependence in squared residuals for GARCH(1,1), and latent-state dependence for Markov switching. We introduce a curve-collapse diagnostic to assess whether <math id="S1.I1.i1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> explains performance more effectively than the raw delay <math id="S1.I1.i1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>. The experiments show that the information captured by <math id="S1.I1.i1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> depends on the mechanism of non-exchangeability. Under AR(1), <math id="S1.I1.i1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> strongly explains overall interval performance. Under GARCH(1,1), it provides a more moderate organization of the raw interval score but more clearly identifies when scale normalization is beneficial or detrimental. Under Markov switching, <math id="S1.I1.i1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> does not produce a strong collapse in overall interval performance, but it does strongly characterize how the benefit of state-dependent normalization changes as the forecast delay grows relative to regime persistence. Complementary mean- and variance-shift experiments examine abrupt changes for which no stationary memory scale is available. Overall, the delay-to-memory ratio allows delays across processes with different time scales to be compared on a common axis. The experiments show that its explanatory power depends on the form of non-exchangeability, but across persistent processes it provides information that the raw horizon <math id="S1.I1.i1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> alone cannot.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Coverage analysis of the <math id="S1.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>-delayed ACI recursion:</span>
We introduce a phase-based representation that decomposes the delayed recursion into <math id="S1.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> interleaved standard-ACI-like sequences (Section <a href="#S4.SS1" title="4.1 Alternative Form of 𝜏-DACI ‣ 4 𝜏-Delayed Adaptive Conformal Inference ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a>). Each phase is updated once every <math id="S1.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> calendar steps, and recombining the phase-wise bounds yields boundedness and a finite-sample long-run coverage bound with explicit dependence on <math id="S1.I1.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> (Sections <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Boundedness of 𝛼_𝑚^(𝜃) ‣ 4 𝜏-Delayed Adaptive Conformal Inference ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>–<a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 Long-term Coverage Guarantees ‣ 4 𝜏-Delayed Adaptive Conformal Inference ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>). We additionally derive an approximate marginal coverage bound under a hidden Markov model (Section <a href="#S4.SS4" title="4.4 Approximate Marginal Coverage ‣ 4 𝜏-Delayed Adaptive Conformal Inference ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a>), relating coverage deviation to distributional change between prediction and target time and to the adaptation rate <math id="S1.I1.i2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>. To our knowledge, no analogous marginal coverage bound or phase-based representation has been established for <math id="S1.I1.i2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>-delayed ACI.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The theoretical analysis shows how delay affects both long-run and marginal coverage, while the simulations show that its practical effect depends on the persistence of temporal dependence and where that persistence appears in the residual process.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Forecasting Setup</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In our forecasting framework, the objective is to predict the target output at a future time <math id="S2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t+\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t+\tau</annotation></semantics></math>, where, for example, <math id="S2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau\in\{5,10,15,20,30,40\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>40</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau\in\{5,10,15,20,30,40\}</annotation></semantics></math> minutes denotes the forecast horizon. At each time step <math id="S2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, the model receives a history of recent sequential observations:</p>
<table id="S2.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<p id="S2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X_{i},Y_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X_{i},Y_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> is the covariate-response pair. This sequence is passed into a fixed forecasting model <math id="S2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu^{\tau}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>μ</mi><mi>τ</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu^{\tau}</annotation></semantics></math>, which outputs a point prediction for the future response:</p>

</div>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Online Split Conformal Prediction</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In the standard split conformal setting, the calibration set is fixed, so the empirical distribution of conformity scores and its associated quantile function remain unchanged throughout deployment. In an online setting, the calibration set evolves as new data becomes available. At each time step <math id="S3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, we observe <math id="S3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and can therefore compute a conformity score <math id="S3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> to assess the accuracy of a past prediction made <math id="S3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> steps earlier. We use the signed residual</p>
<table id="S3.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="S_{t}=Y_{t}-\mu^{\tau}(X_{t-h-\tau:t-\tau},Y_{t-h-\tau:t-\tau})=Y_{t}-\hat{Y}_{t}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>μ</mi><mi>τ</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{t}=Y_{t}-\mu^{\tau}(X_{t-h-\tau:t-\tau},Y_{t-h-\tau:t-\tau})=Y_{t}-\hat{Y}_{t},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">which yields a possibly asymmetric interval that can adapt to skewed or directionally biased residual distributions. The absolute residual <math id="S3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|Y_{t}-\hat{Y}_{t}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|Y_{t}-\hat{Y}_{t}|</annotation></semantics></math> is a common alternative that instead yields a symmetric interval, and either choice is compatible with everything that follows. To assess model performance over time, we maintain a sliding window of the most recent <math id="S3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> conformity scores. We refer to <math id="S3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> both as the set of these <math id="S3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> scores and as the empirical distribution formed by assigning equal mass to each score:</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S3.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{t}=\{S_{t-R+1},S_{t-R+2},\ldots,S_{t}\}\quad\text{or equivalently}\quad\mathcal{D}_{t}=\frac{1}{R}\sum_{i=t-R+1}^{t}\delta_{S_{i}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mtext>or equivalently</mtext><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>R</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mi>t</mi></munderover><msub><mi>δ</mi><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{t}=\{S_{t-R+1},S_{t-R+2},\ldots,S_{t}\}\quad\text{or equivalently}\quad\mathcal{D}_{t}=\frac{1}{R}\sum_{i=t-R+1}^{t}\delta_{S_{i}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{S_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{S_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the Dirac delta function centered at <math id="S3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>. Then, for each time step <math id="S3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, the time-varying quantile function <math id="S3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{Q}_{t}(p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{Q}_{t}(p)</annotation></semantics></math> is defined as:</p>
<table id="S3.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E3.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\hat{Q}_{t}(p,\mathcal{D}_{t}):=\inf\left\{s:\frac{1}{R}\sum_{i=t-R+1}^{t}\mathbbm{1}\{S_{i}\leq s\}\geq p\right\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">:=</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em" movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">inf</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>R</mi></mfrac><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mi>t</mi></munderover><mn>𝟙</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{Q}_{t}(p,\mathcal{D}_{t}):=\inf\left\{s:\frac{1}{R}\sum_{i=t-R+1}^{t}\mathbbm{1}\{S_{i}\leq s\}\geq p\right\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Using this quantile function, the prediction set for <math id="S3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y_{t+\tau}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y_{t+\tau}</annotation></semantics></math> constructed at time <math id="S3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> is</p>
<table id="S3.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathcal{C}}_{t+\tau}^{\tau}(\alpha)=\left[\hat{Y}_{t+\tau}+\hat{Q}_{t}(\alpha/2,\mathcal{D}_{t}),\ \hat{Y}_{t+\tau}+\hat{Q}_{t}(1-\alpha/2,\mathcal{D}_{t})\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mi>τ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.667em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathcal{C}}_{t+\tau}^{\tau}(\alpha)=\left[\hat{Y}_{t+\tau}+\hat{Q}_{t}(\alpha/2,\mathcal{D}_{t}),\ \hat{Y}_{t+\tau}+\hat{Q}_{t}(1-\alpha/2,\mathcal{D}_{t})\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The prediction set <math id="S3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathcal{C}}_{t+\tau}^{\tau}(\alpha)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mi>τ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathcal{C}}_{t+\tau}^{\tau}(\alpha)</annotation></semantics></math> is constructed using conformity scores computed from past predictions at times <math id="S3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t^{\prime}\leq t-\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t^{\prime}\leq t-\tau</annotation></semantics></math>, once the corresponding outcomes <math id="S3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y_{t^{\prime}+\tau}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Y</mi><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y_{t^{\prime}+\tau}</annotation></semantics></math> have been observed. In other words, the residuals used to calibrate the quantile function <math id="S3.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{Q}_{t}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{Q}_{t}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> reflect prediction errors made by the forecast model at least <math id="S3.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> time steps ago. These residuals are then used to construct the prediction interval around the current forecast <math id="S3.p4.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\hat{Y}_{t+\tau}=\mu^{\tau}(X_{t-h:t},Y_{t-h:t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>μ</mi><mi>τ</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{Y}_{t+\tau}=\mu^{\tau}(X_{t-h:t},Y_{t-h:t})</annotation></semantics></math>. As a result, when the forecast horizon <math id="S3.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> is large, the quantile function may be slow to adapt to recent changes in the data distribution, potentially leading to miscalibrated or suboptimal prediction intervals (lag in adaptation). This introduces a tradeoff between forecast horizon and calibration responsiveness in rapidly evolving environments. 
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Algorithm <a href="#alg1" title="Algorithm 1 ‣ 3 Online Split Conformal Prediction ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> gives the full procedure for constructing prediction sets online. Assuming observations begin at <math id="S3.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=1</annotation></semantics></math>, the first forecast is generated at <math id="S3.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=h+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=h+1</annotation></semantics></math>, and the corresponding conformity score becomes available at <math id="S3.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=h+\tau+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=h+\tau+1</annotation></semantics></math>. Fitting <math id="S3.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{Q}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{Q}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> requires a window of <math id="S3.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> residuals, collected by <math id="S3.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=h+\tau+R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=h+\tau+R</annotation></semantics></math>. We therefore define <math id="S3.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{0}=h+\tau+R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{0}=h+\tau+R</annotation></semantics></math> and perform conformal updates for <math id="S3.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=t_{0}+1,\ldots,T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=t_{0}+1,\ldots,T</annotation></semantics></math>. For notational simplicity, in the algorithms that follow, we re-index time so that <math id="S3.p5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{0}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{0}=0</annotation></semantics></math>.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<figure id="alg1" class="ltx_float ltx_float_algorithm ltx_framed ltx_framed_top">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_float"><span id="alg1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Algorithm 1</span> </span> Prediction Set Estimator (PSE)</figcaption>
<div id="alg1.4" class="ltx_listing ltx_framed ltx_framed_topbottom ltx_listing">
<div id="alg1.l1" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">1:</span></span>
            
            
          <span id="alg1.l1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Input:</span> <math id="alg1.l1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="(X_{t-h-\tau:t},Y_{t-h-\tau:t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X_{t-h-\tau:t},Y_{t-h-\tau:t})</annotation></semantics></math>, forecasting model <math id="alg1.l1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu^{\tau}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>μ</mi><mi>τ</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu^{\tau}</annotation></semantics></math>, miscoverage level <math id="alg1.l1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha\in(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha\in(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math>, calibration set <math id="alg1.l1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{t-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{t-1}</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l2" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">2:</span></span>
            
            
          Compute point prediction: <math id="alg1.l2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\hat{Y}_{t+\tau}\leftarrow\mu^{\tau}(X_{t-h:t},Y_{t-h:t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><msup><mi>μ</mi><mi>τ</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{Y}_{t+\tau}\leftarrow\mu^{\tau}(X_{t-h:t},Y_{t-h:t})</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l3" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">3:</span></span>
            
            
          Compute past prediction: <math id="alg1.l3.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\hat{Y}_{t}\leftarrow\mu^{\tau}(X_{t-h-\tau:t-\tau},Y_{t-h-\tau:t-\tau})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><msup><mi>μ</mi><mi>τ</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{Y}_{t}\leftarrow\mu^{\tau}(X_{t-h-\tau:t-\tau},Y_{t-h-\tau:t-\tau})</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l4" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">4:</span></span>
            
            
          Compute conformity score: <math id="alg1.l4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{t}\leftarrow Y_{t}-\hat{Y}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{t}\leftarrow Y_{t}-\hat{Y}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l5" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">5:</span></span>
            
            
          Update calibration set: <math id="alg1.l5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{t}\leftarrow\{S_{t-R+1},\ldots,S_{t}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{t}\leftarrow\{S_{t-R+1},\ldots,S_{t}\}</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l6" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l6.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">6:</span></span>
            
            
          Fit empirical quantile function:

<table id="S3.Ex3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\hat{Q}_{t}(p,\mathcal{D}_{t}):=\inf\left\{s:\frac{1}{R}\sum_{i=t-R+1}^{t}\mathbbm{1}\{S_{i}\leq s\}\geq p\right\}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">:=</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em" movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">inf</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>R</mi></mfrac><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mi>t</mi></munderover><mn>𝟙</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{Q}_{t}(p,\mathcal{D}_{t}):=\inf\left\{s:\frac{1}{R}\sum_{i=t-R+1}^{t}\mathbbm{1}\{S_{i}\leq s\}\geq p\right\}</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l7" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l7.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">7:</span></span>
            
            
          Compute prediction interval:

<div id="alg1.l8" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l8.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">8:</span></span>
            
            
          <span id="alg1.l8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">return</span> <math id="alg1.l8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathcal{C}}_{t+\tau}^{\tau}(\alpha)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mi>τ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathcal{C}}_{t+\tau}^{\tau}(\alpha)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="alg1.l8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>

</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span><math id="S4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>-Delayed Adaptive Conformal Inference</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Adaptive Conformal Inference (ACI) addresses the challenge of making valid predictions in non-exchangeable, online environments by treating the coverage level as a tunable parameter that can be learned and updated over time. We begin by defining the miscoverage rate, which quantifies the probability that the true target value <math id="S4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> lies outside the prediction set generated <math id="S4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> time steps earlier. Specifically, the miscoverage rate at time <math id="S4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> is given by:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{t}(\alpha):=\mathbb{P}\left(Y_{t}\notin\hat{C}_{t}^{\tau}(\alpha)\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mi>ℙ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∉</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>C</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mi>τ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{t}(\alpha):=\mathbb{P}\left(Y_{t}\notin\hat{C}_{t}^{\tau}(\alpha)\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{C}_{t}^{\tau}(\alpha)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>C</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mi>τ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{C}_{t}^{\tau}(\alpha)</annotation></semantics></math> is the prediction set formed at time <math id="S4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t-\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t-\tau</annotation></semantics></math> for the target <math id="S4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>. When using the signed residual, the miscoverage rate becomes <math id="S4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{t}(\alpha)=\mathbb{P}(S_{t}(y)&lt;\hat{Q}_{t-\tau}(\alpha/2)\ \text{or}\ S_{t}(y)&gt;\hat{Q}_{t-\tau}(1-\alpha/2))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ℙ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.500em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>or</mtext><mo lspace="0.500em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{t}(\alpha)=\mathbb{P}(S_{t}(y)&lt;\hat{Q}_{t-\tau}(\alpha/2)\ \text{or}\ S_{t}(y)&gt;\hat{Q}_{t-\tau}(1-\alpha/2))</annotation></semantics></math>.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In our time-series application, the data are non-exchangeable, therefore, the miscoverage rate <math id="S4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{t}(\alpha)\neq\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{t}(\alpha)\neq\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>. However, as noted by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gibbs and Candès (2021)</a></cite>, if the conformity scores used to define the quantile function <math id="S4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{Q}_{t-\tau}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{Q}_{t-\tau}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> capture the bulk of the distribution, then it is possible to find a time-varying level <math id="S4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{t}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{t}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="S4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{t}(\alpha_{t}^{*})=\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{t}(\alpha_{t}^{*})=\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>, or approximately so. We define the optimal miscoverage level <math id="S4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{t}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{t}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> as the largest level for which the prediction set generated at time <math id="S4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t-\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t-\tau</annotation></semantics></math> would have yielded valid coverage at time <math id="S4.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S4.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{t}^{*}:=\sup\left\{\beta\in[0,1]:\mathcal{M}_{t}(\beta)\leq\alpha\right\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo rspace="0.1389em">:=</mo><mrow><mo lspace="0.1389em" movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">sup</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{t}^{*}:=\sup\left\{\beta\in[0,1]:\mathcal{M}_{t}(\beta)\leq\alpha\right\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">This definition relies on the assumption that the quantile function <math id="S4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{Q}_{t-\tau}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{Q}_{t-\tau}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous, non-decreasing, and satisfies the boundary conditions <math id="S4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{Q}_{t-\tau}(0)=-\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{Q}_{t-\tau}(0)=-\infty</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{Q}_{t-\tau}(1)=\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{Q}_{t-\tau}(1)=\infty</annotation></semantics></math>. Our definition of the quantile in Equation <a href="#S3.E3" title="In 3 Online Split Conformal Prediction ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> satisfies these assumptions once it is smoothed to eliminate discontinuities, extrapolated to extend to <math id="S4.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\infty</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, and adjusted to handle tied scores appropriately. Since the true miscoverage rate is unknown in practice, we estimate <math id="S4.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{t}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{t}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> adaptively using a delayed online update rule:</p>
<table id="S4.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E6.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\alpha_{t+\tau}=\alpha_{t}+\gamma\left(\alpha-\texttt{err}_{t}\right)\quad\text{where}\quad\texttt{err}_{t}=\mathbbm{1}\left\{Y_{t}\notin\hat{\mathcal{C}}_{t}^{\tau}(\alpha_{t})\right\}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>γ</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">err</mtext><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>where</mtext><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">err</mtext><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>𝟙</mn><mrow><mo>{</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∉</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mi>τ</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{t+\tau}=\alpha_{t}+\gamma\left(\alpha-\texttt{err}_{t}\right)\quad\text{where}\quad\texttt{err}_{t}=\mathbbm{1}\left\{Y_{t}\notin\hat{\mathcal{C}}_{t}^{\tau}(\alpha_{t})\right\},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p4.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\texttt{err}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">err</mtext><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\texttt{err}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is a binary indicator that records whether the prediction set constructed at time <math id="S4.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t-\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t-\tau</annotation></semantics></math> failed to cover the true observation <math id="S4.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S4.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> is a fixed step-size. The updated level <math id="S4.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{t+\tau}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{t+\tau}</annotation></semantics></math> is then used to construct the prediction set <math id="S4.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathcal{C}}_{t+\tau}^{\tau}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mi>τ</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathcal{C}}_{t+\tau}^{\tau}</annotation></semantics></math> at time <math id="S4.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S4.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y_{t+\tau}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y_{t+\tau}</annotation></semantics></math>, ensuring temporal alignment between the prediction and the adaptive correction based on prior forecast performance. If the prediction set undercovers (i.e., <math id="S4.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\texttt{err}_{t}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">err</mtext><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\texttt{err}_{t}=1</annotation></semantics></math>), <math id="S4.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is reduced to increase the width of future intervals. If the prediction set overcovers (i.e., <math id="S4.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\texttt{err}_{t}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">err</mtext><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\texttt{err}_{t}=0</annotation></semantics></math>), <math id="S4.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is increased to reduce the interval width. We refer to the update rule in Eq <a href="#S4.E6" title="In 4 𝜏-Delayed Adaptive Conformal Inference ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> as <math id="S4.p4.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>-Delayed Adaptive Conformal Inference (<math id="S4.p4.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>-DACI). When the forecast horizon is set to <math id="S4.p4.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=1</annotation></semantics></math>, we recover the original ACI formulation proposed by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gibbs and Candès (2021)</a></cite>. <math id="S4.p4.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>-DACI is showcased in Algorithm <a href="#alg2" title="Algorithm 2 ‣ 4 𝜏-Delayed Adaptive Conformal Inference ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>

<div id="alg2.l11" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg2.l11.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">11:</span></span>
            
            
            Enqueue: <math id="alg2.l11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q.\texttt{append}(\hat{\mathcal{C}}_{t+\tau}^{\tau},\alpha^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">append</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mi>τ</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>α</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q.\texttt{append}(\hat{\mathcal{C}}_{t+\tau}^{\tau},\alpha^{*})</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg2.l12" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg2.l12.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">12:</span></span>
            
            
          <span id="alg2.l12.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">end</span> <span id="alg2.l12.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">for</span>
