<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Alternative Form of <math id="S4.SS1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>-DACI</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Although the delayed update is naturally expressed in the global time index <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, this representation obscures an important structural feature of the recursion. Since <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{t+\tau}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{t+\tau}</annotation></semantics></math> depends on <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, the full sequence can be viewed as <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> interleaved subsequences, each evolving at time points separated by <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> steps. Reindexing these subsequences by phase makes this structure explicit. Within each phase, the delayed recursion becomes an ordinary one-step ACI update, with no explicit delay in the update index. This reformulation is useful theoretically because it allows standard ACI arguments, including boundedness and long-run coverage analysis, to be applied separately to each phase and then combined to recover statements for the full delayed process. To see this concretely, consider the case where <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=5</annotation></semantics></math>. In this setting, the update at time <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=6</annotation></semantics></math> depends only on <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and is independent of <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{2},\alpha_{3},\alpha_{4}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{2},\alpha_{3},\alpha_{4},</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{5}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{6}=\alpha_{1}+\gamma(\alpha-\texttt{err}_{1})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">err</mtext><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{6}=\alpha_{1}+\gamma(\alpha-\texttt{err}_{1}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">More generally, for a fixed phase <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>, connected updates occur at times spaced exactly <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> steps apart: <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta=1</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=1,6,11,16,\dots" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=1,6,11,16,\dots</annotation></semantics></math>; <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta=2</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=2,7,12,17,\dots" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>17</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=2,7,12,17,\dots</annotation></semantics></math>; and so on through <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta=5</annotation></semantics></math>, giving <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=5,10,15,20,\dots" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=5,10,15,20,\dots</annotation></semantics></math>. Varying <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> over <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{1,\dots,\tau\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{1,\dots,\tau\}</annotation></semantics></math> spans all time indices, ensuring that every <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> belongs to exactly one phase. This motivates reindexing the process using two indices:</p>
<ol id="S4.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S4.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">a <span id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">phase index</span> <math id="S4.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta\in\{1,\dots,\tau\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta\in\{1,\dots,\tau\}</annotation></semantics></math>, identifying the position within the cycle, and</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">an <span id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">update index</span> <math id="S4.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math>, counting how many updates have occurred within that phase.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S4.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 4.1 Alternative Form of 𝜏-DACI ‣ 4 𝜏-Delayed Adaptive Conformal Inference ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> illustrates how global time indices are uniquely mapped to pairs of phase <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> and update index <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>. Every time step <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> can then be uniquely represented by a pair <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\theta,m)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\theta,m)</annotation></semantics></math>, which forms the basis of the phase-based representation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S4.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{\theta}(m):=t_{0}+\theta+(m-1)\tau." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{\theta}(m):=t_{0}+\theta+(m-1)\tau.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">This implies</p>
<table id="S4.Ex8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S4.T1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 1</span>: </span><span id="S4.T1.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Mapping of global time index <math id="S4.T1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{\theta}(m)=t_{0}+\theta+(m-1)\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{\theta}(m)=t_{0}+\theta+(m-1)\tau</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S4.T1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=5</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.T1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{0}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{0}=0</annotation></semantics></math> .
Each row corresponds to a fixed phase <math id="S4.T1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>, and each column to an update index <math id="S4.T1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">so the update rule (Equation <a href="#S4.E6" title="In 4 𝜏-Delayed Adaptive Conformal Inference ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>) at time <math id="S4.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{\theta}(m)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{\theta}(m)</annotation></semantics></math> becomes</p>
<table id="S4.Ex9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Defining phase-wise sequences</p>

</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.p5.2" class="ltx_p">we obtain the compact <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>-DACI form:</p>

<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">In <math id="S4.SS1.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>-space, each phase updates once every <math id="S4.SS1.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> steps, whereas in <math id="S4.SS1.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>-space (after decoupling) each sequence updates at every iteration, exactly like standard ACI. This preserves the link to the actual time index while removing the explicit delay from the update rule, enabling the direct application of standard ACI analysis tools phase-wise.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">For <math id="S4.SS1.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=t_{0}+1,\dots,T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=t_{0}+1,\dots,T</annotation></semantics></math>, we define the phase of a time step <math id="S4.SS1.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> by</p>
<table id="S4.Ex11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t-t_{0})\bmod\tau=\theta,\quad\theta\in\{1,\dots,\tau\}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(t-t_{0})\bmod\tau=\theta,\quad\theta\in\{1,\dots,\tau\},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.p7.2" class="ltx_p">with the convention that <math id="S4.SS1.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta=\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta=\tau</annotation></semantics></math> when the remainder is zero. The initial time corresponds to <math id="S4.SS1.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta=1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS1.p7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m=1</annotation></semantics></math>, which gives <math id="S4.SS1.p7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{1}(1)=t_{0}+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{1}(1)=t_{0}+1</annotation></semantics></math>. The number <math id="S4.SS1.p7.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> counts how many updates occur before or at the terminal time <math id="S4.SS1.p7.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> in phase <math id="S4.SS1.p7.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>. This means we are looking for all integers <math id="S4.SS1.p7.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> such that</p>
<table id="S4.Ex12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex12.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="t_{0}+\theta+(m-1)\tau\leq T\quad\iff\quad m\leq\frac{T-(t_{0}+\theta)}{\tau}+1." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">⇔</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>τ</mi></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{0}+\theta+(m-1)\tau\leq T\quad\iff\quad m\leq\frac{T-(t_{0}+\theta)}{\tau}+1.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.p7.3" class="ltx_p">Since <math id="S4.SS1.p7.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> must be a positive integer, the largest allowable value of <math id="S4.SS1.p7.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> is obtained by taking the integer part (floor) of the right-hand side. Therefore,</p>
<table id="S4.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{\theta}=\left\lfloor\frac{T-(t_{0}+\theta)}{\tau}\right\rfloor+1." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>⌊</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>τ</mi></mfrac><mo>⌋</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{\theta}=\left\lfloor\frac{T-(t_{0}+\theta)}{\tau}\right\rfloor+1.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p8.1" class="ltx_p">The last phase index can be identified from the remainder when <math id="S4.SS1.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T-t_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T-t_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> is divided by <math id="S4.SS1.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta^{\star}=(T-t_{0})\bmod\tau," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta^{\star}=(T-t_{0})\bmod\tau,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.p8.2" class="ltx_p">with the convention <math id="S4.SS1.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta^{\star}=\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta^{\star}=\tau</annotation></semantics></math> when the remainder is zero. This captures the fact that updates proceed in cycles of length <math id="S4.SS1.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S4.SS1.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> marks the phase of the final update time within the last (possibly incomplete) cycle.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Boundedness of <math id="S4.SS2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}</annotation></semantics></math></h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Establishing bounds on <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}</annotation></semantics></math> is essential for ensuring the stability of the <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>-DACI update process. Boundedness guarantees that the miscoverage levels remain within a controlled range, preventing divergence that could lead to unstable or degenerate prediction sets. For each fixed <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>, the phase-wise sequence <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}</annotation></semantics></math> obeys the same Robbins–Monro style update as in standard ACI, and Appendix <a href="#A1.SS1" title="A.1 Boundedness of 𝛼_𝑚^(𝜃) ‣ Appendix A Proofs for Coverage Guarantees Under Delayed Feedback ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.1</span></a> shows that for all <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="S4.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}\in[-\gamma,\,1+\gamma]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn> 1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}\in[-\gamma,\,1+\gamma].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">This bound follows the same basic argument as Lemma 4.1 of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gibbs and Candès (2021)</a></cite>. If <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}</annotation></semantics></math> moves beyond either boundary, the two-sided prediction interval induced by the signed-residual construction becomes degenerate: it equals all of <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℝ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math> when <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}&lt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}&lt;0</annotation></semantics></math> and is empty when <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}&gt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}&gt;1</annotation></semantics></math>. Consequently, the miscoverage indicator <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{m}^{(\theta)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>e</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{m}^{(\theta)}</annotation></semantics></math> is forced to take the value that drives the subsequent update back toward the interior of the interval. Relative to the standard ACI argument, two modifications are required in the delayed setting. First, the relevant quantiles are those fitted at time <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{\theta}(m-1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{\theta}(m-1)</annotation></semantics></math> rather than at <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t-1</annotation></semantics></math>, reflecting the <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>-step delay. Second, the argument is formulated in terms of a two-sided prediction interval rather than a one-sided threshold, as required by the signed-residual construction.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Long-term Coverage Guarantees</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We now state the long-term coverage guarantee for <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>-DACI, obtained by combining the phase-wise bound of Equation <a href="#S4.E10" title="In 4.2 Boundedness of 𝛼_𝑚^(𝜃) ‣ 4 𝜏-Delayed Adaptive Conformal Inference ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> with the phase-recombination argument of Appendix <a href="#A1.SS2" title="A.2 Long-Term Coverage Guarantees ‣ Appendix A Proofs for Coverage Guarantees Under Delayed Feedback ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.2</span></a>, following the reasoning of Proposition 4.1 in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gibbs and Candès (2021)</a></cite>. Appendix <a href="#A1.SS2" title="A.2 Long-Term Coverage Guarantees ‣ Appendix A Proofs for Coverage Guarantees Under Delayed Feedback ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.2</span></a> shows that</p>
<table id="S4.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left|\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\texttt{err}_{t}-\alpha\right|\;\leq\;\frac{1}{\gamma\,T}\sum_{\theta=1}^{\tau}\max\{\alpha^{(\theta)}_{1},\;1-\alpha^{(\theta)}_{1}\}\;+\;\frac{\tau}{T}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>T</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">err</mtext><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.280em">|</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>τ</mi></munderover><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn> 1</mn><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.502em">+</mo><mfrac><mi>τ</mi><mi>T</mi></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\texttt{err}_{t}-\alpha\right|\;\leq\;\frac{1}{\gamma\,T}\sum_{\theta=1}^{\tau}\max\{\alpha^{(\theta)}_{1},\;1-\alpha^{(\theta)}_{1}\}\;+\;\frac{\tau}{T}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">In particular, <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\texttt{err}_{t}\to\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>T</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></msubsup><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">err</mtext><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\texttt{err}_{t}\to\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> almost surely as <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The bound in (<a href="#S4.E11" title="In 4.3 Long-term Coverage Guarantees ‣ 4 𝜏-Delayed Adaptive Conformal Inference ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>) is <em id="S4.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">distribution-free</em>: it makes no assumptions on the data-generating process beyond the phase-wise boundedness of the iterates established in Equation <a href="#S4.E10" title="In 4.2 Boundedness of 𝛼_𝑚^(𝜃) ‣ 4 𝜏-Delayed Adaptive Conformal Inference ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>. When <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=1</annotation></semantics></math>, there is a single phase with <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{1}=T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{1}=T</annotation></semantics></math>, and (<a href="#S4.E11" title="In 4.3 Long-term Coverage Guarantees ‣ 4 𝜏-Delayed Adaptive Conformal Inference ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>) reduces exactly to the bound in Proposition 4.1 of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gibbs and Candès (2021)</a></cite>. The deviation from the target coverage <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> decreases as <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> grows but is generally larger for longer forecast horizons (larger <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>), and also depends on the quality of the initialization <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha^{(\theta)}_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha^{(\theta)}_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>Approximate Marginal Coverage</h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The long-run bound in Equation (<a href="#S4.E11" title="In 4.3 Long-term Coverage Guarantees ‣ 4 𝜏-Delayed Adaptive Conformal Inference ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>) ensures that, on average over time, the empirical miscoverage (<math id="S4.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\texttt{err}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>T</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></msubsup><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">err</mtext><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\texttt{err}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>) approaches the target level <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>. However, this guarantee does not describe the behavior of the marginal coverage at a single time step. To study instantaneous performance, we adopt the same probabilistic modeling framework as <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gibbs and Candès (2021)</a></cite>, generalized here to the <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>-delayed setting.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Problem setup:</h4>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We model the data as arising from a hidden Markov model. Let <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{A_{t}\}_{t\in\mathbb{N}}\subseteq\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℕ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>⊆</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{A_{t}\}_{t\in\mathbb{N}}\subseteq\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the latent environment process. For the adaptive sequence <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\alpha_{t}\}_{t\in\mathbb{N}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℕ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\alpha_{t}\}_{t\in\mathbb{N}}</annotation></semantics></math>, with values evolving within the bounded range <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{t}\in[-\gamma,\,1+\gamma]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn> 1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{t}\in[-\gamma,\,1+\gamma]</annotation></semantics></math>, we define the true conditional marginal miscoverage at time <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> in environment <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M(\alpha_{t}\mid A_{t}):=\mathbb{P}\!\left(Y_{t}\notin\hat{\mathcal{C}}^{\tau}_{t}(\alpha_{t})\,\middle|\,A_{t}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.441em;" width="0.441em"><mi>ℙ</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∉</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mi>τ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0.170em" stretchy="true">|</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M(\alpha_{t}\mid A_{t}):=\mathbb{P}\!\left(Y_{t}\notin\hat{\mathcal{C}}^{\tau}_{t}(\alpha_{t})\,\middle|\,A_{t}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In this setting, we assume that the process <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{(\alpha_{t},A_{t},\texttt{err}_{t})\}_{t\in\mathbb{N}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">err</mtext><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℕ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{(\alpha_{t},A_{t},\texttt{err}_{t})\}_{t\in\mathbb{N}}</annotation></semantics></math> is stationary, with
marginal stationary distribution <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\alpha_{t},A_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\alpha_{t},A_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[-\gamma,\,1+\gamma]\times\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn> 1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-\gamma,\,1+\gamma]\times\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math>. In particular, the initialization
<math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\alpha_{1},A_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\alpha_{1},A_{1})</annotation></semantics></math> is drawn from <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>. This stationarity assumption greatly simplifies the characterization of the behavior of the error indicators <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\texttt{err}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">err</mtext><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\texttt{err}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>. Finally, we impose two technical conditions:</p>
<ol id="S4.I2" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S4.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S4.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lipschitz continuity:</span> There exists a constant <math id="S4.I2.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{Lip}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{Lip}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> such that for all <math id="S4.I2.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a\in\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a\in\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math> and all <math id="S4.I2.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2}\in[-\gamma,\,1+\gamma]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn> 1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2}\in[-\gamma,\,1+\gamma]</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="S4.Ex14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\big|M(\alpha_{2}\mid a)-M(\alpha_{1}\mid a)\big|\leq L_{Lip}\,|\alpha_{2}-\alpha_{1}|." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\big|M(\alpha_{2}\mid a)-M(\alpha_{1}\mid a)\big|\leq L_{Lip}\,|\alpha_{2}-\alpha_{1}|.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S4.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Existence of an optimal level:</span> For each <math id="S4.I2.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a\in\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a\in\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math>, there exists a unique <math id="S4.I2.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha^{*}_{a}\in(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>a</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha^{*}_{a}\in(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math> such that</p>
<table id="S4.Ex15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M(\alpha^{*}_{a}\mid a)=\alpha." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>a</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M(\alpha^{*}_{a}\mid a)=\alpha.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="S4.I2.i2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">We refer to <math id="S4.I2.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha^{*}_{A_{t}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>α</mi><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha^{*}_{A_{t}}</annotation></semantics></math> as the <em id="S4.I2.i2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">optimal miscoverage level</em> at time <math id="S4.I2.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e., the value that would have achieved exact target coverage under environment <math id="S4.I2.i2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Main result:</h4>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">With these assumptions in place, we can quantify the deviation of the instantaneous marginal miscoverage from the target level. Specifically, Appendix <a href="#A1.SS3" title="A.3 Approximate Marginal Coverage ‣ Appendix A Proofs for Coverage Guarantees Under Delayed Feedback ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.3</span></a> shows that under stationarity, the expected squared deviation satisfies</p>
<table id="S4.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}\!\left[\big(M(\alpha_{t}\mid rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo
