encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}\!\left[\big(M(\alpha_{t}\mid A_{t})-\alpha\big)^{2}\right]\;\leq\;\frac{L_{Lip}(1+\gamma)}{\gamma}\,\mathbb{E}\!\left[\big|\alpha^{*}_{A_{t+\tau}}-\alpha^{*}_{A_{t}}\big|\right]+\frac{L_{Lip}}{2}\,\gamma,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">where the expectation is taken with respect to the stationary distribution of <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\alpha_{t},A_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\alpha_{t},A_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The bound decomposes into two terms: the first measures the <em id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">distribution shift</em> of the latent environment across <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> steps, captured by the expected difference between the optimal levels <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha^{*}_{A_{t}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>α</mi><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha^{*}_{A_{t}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha^{*}_{A_{t+\tau}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>α</mi><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha^{*}_{A_{t+\tau}}</annotation></semantics></math>, while the second reflects the <em id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">adaptation penalty</em>, which grows linearly with the step-size <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>. When <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=1</annotation></semantics></math>, the expression reduces to the approximate marginal coverage bound of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gibbs and Candès (2021)</a></cite>; the delayed setting introduces an explicit dependence on shift over <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> steps. Choosing</p>
<table id="S4.Ex16" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma_{\mathrm{opt}}=\sqrt{2\,\mathbb{E}\!\left[\,|\alpha^{*}_{A_{t+\tau}}-\alpha^{*}_{A_{t}}|\,\right]}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mi>opt</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mpadded style="width:0.497em;" width="0.497em"><mi>𝔼</mi></mpadded><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.170em">[</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>α</mi><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∗</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_{\mathrm{opt}}=\sqrt{2\,\mathbb{E}\!\left[\,|\alpha^{*}_{A_{t+\tau}}-\alpha^{*}_{A_{t}}|\,\right]}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.2" class="ltx_p">minimizes the right-hand side of the bound in <a href="#S4.E12" title="In Main result: ‣ 4.4 Approximate Marginal Coverage ‣ 4 𝜏-Delayed Adaptive Conformal Inference ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> and therefore yields the optimal
tradeoff between adaptation and stability.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Evaluation Metrics</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Coverage alone does not provide a complete assessment of a conformal forecasting method. In particular, the nominal coverage level can be attained by producing arbitrarily wide prediction intervals that cover all observations without being informative. Also, measures of aggregate empirical coverage may obscure periods of substantial under- or overcoverage. We therefore evaluate our methods along complementary dimensions that capture overall calibration, the temporal stability of coverage, and the cost of calibration in terms of predictive sharpness (i.e., interval width).</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Empirical coverage:</h4>

<div id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We report the empirical coverage</p>
<table id="S5.E13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.E13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathrm{err}_{t}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>T</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover><msub><mi>err</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathrm{err}_{t},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(13)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{err}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>err</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{err}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the miscoverage indicator defined in (<a href="#S4.E6" title="In 4 𝜏-Delayed Adaptive Conformal Inference ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>). A well-calibrated method should achieve empirical coverage close to the nominal target <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Worst-case local coverage error:</h4>

<div id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Global empirical coverage can mask temporal clustering of miscoverage. For example, a period of severe undercoverage following a distribution shift may have little effect on the overall average if it is preceded or followed by a long period of stable coverage. To quantify such local deviations from the target, we report the worst-case local coverage error (LCE) over all contiguous windows of length <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S5.E14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.E14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LCE}_{k}:=\max_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq j\leq T-k+1\end{subarray}}\left|\alpha-\frac{1}{k}\sum_{t=j}^{j+k-1}\mathrm{err}_{t}\right|." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>LCE</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><munder><mi>max</mi><mtable><mtr><mtd><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></munder><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>k</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munderover><msub><mi>err</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LCE}_{k}:=\max_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq j\leq T-k+1\end{subarray}}\left|\alpha-\frac{1}{k}\sum_{t=j}^{j+k-1}\mathrm{err}_{t}\right|.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(14)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Here, the average miscoverage rate within each window is compared with the nominal miscoverage level <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>. Smaller values of <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LCE}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>LCE</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LCE}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> indicate that calibration is maintained more consistently over time, whereas larger values reveal intervals in which the method exhibits substantial local under- or overcoverage. Worst-case local coverage error is evaluated over windows of length <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\in\{100,\allowbreak 250\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>100,250</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\in\{100,\allowbreak 250\}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Interval score:</h4>

<div id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Coverage can be increased by widening prediction intervals, but this comes at the expense of informativeness. To evaluate the trade-off between calibration and sharpness, we report the interval score (IS) at level <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S5.E15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.E15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{IS}_{\alpha}\left([\hat{l}_{t},\hat{u}_{t}],Y_{t}\right):=\left(\hat{u}_{t}-\hat{l}_{t}\right)+\frac{2}{\alpha}\left(\hat{l}_{t}-Y_{t}\right)_{+}+\frac{2}{\alpha}\left(Y_{t}-\hat{u}_{t}\right)_{+}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>IS</mi><mi>α</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>l</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>u</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>u</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>l</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mi>α</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>l</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mi>α</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>u</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{IS}_{\alpha}\left([\hat{l}_{t},\hat{u}_{t}],Y_{t}\right):=\left(\hat{u}_{t}-\hat{l}_{t}\right)+\frac{2}{\alpha}\left(\hat{l}_{t}-Y_{t}\right)_{+}+\frac{2}{\alpha}\left(Y_{t}-\hat{u}_{t}\right)_{+},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(15)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x)_{+}=\max(x,0)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x)_{+}=\max(x,0)</annotation></semantics></math>. When <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> lies within the prediction interval, IS reduces to the interval width <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left(\hat{u}_{t}-\hat{l}_{t}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>u</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>l</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\hat{u}_{t}-\hat{l}_{t}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>. When the interval fails to cover <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, IS additionally penalizes the magnitude of the miss, with the penalty scaled by <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2/\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2/\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus, lower interval scores are better, and correspond to prediction intervals that are simultaneously narrow and well calibrated. We report the time-averaged interval score,</p>
<table id="S5.E16" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.E16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathrm{IS}_{\alpha}\left([\hat{l}_{t},\hat{u}_{t}],Y_{t}\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>T</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover><mrow><msub><mi>IS</mi><mi>α</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>l</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>u</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathrm{IS}_{\alpha}\left([\hat{l}_{t},\hat{u}_{t}],Y_{t}\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(16)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.3" class="ltx_p">as our primary measure of predictive efficiency.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Simulated Residual Processes and Diagnostic Framework</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate <math id="S6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>-DACI using directly simulated residual sequences
<math id="S6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon_{1},\ldots,\varepsilon_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ε</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ε</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon_{1},\ldots,\varepsilon_{T}</annotation></semantics></math>. This approach avoids introducing variation and un-needed complexity from a separate covariate–response model and its associated fitting procedure. Simulating sequences of residuals also allows the temporal dependence, persistence, and distributional dynamics of the residual process to be controlled independently. The resulting experiments isolate how these features interact with the feedback delay <math id="S6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>. We consider six residual families, each designed to represent a distinct mechanism through which the exchangeability assumption may fail. The Gaussian family serves as an exchangeable reference case, while the remaining families introduce temporal dependence, heteroskedasticity, or distributional shift.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Two complementary diagnostics are used to evaluate the residual families. For the three families in which non-exchangeability arises from a persistent, time-varying process — AR(1), GARCH(1,1), and Markov-switching — we study whether the effect of delay can be summarized by a <em id="S6.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">delay-to-memory ratio</em> <math id="S6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=\tau/L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=\tau/L</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S6.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> is a process-specific memory length measuring the time scale over which historical residual information remains informative about future residuals. We assess this using a <em id="S6.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">curve-collapse diagnostic</em>. For each candidate horizontal-axis variable, <math id="S6.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S6.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>, we pool across persistence configurations the interval scores attained at the selected step size <math id="S6.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>γ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math>. <math id="S6.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>γ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> is chosen using a coverage-aware criterion that approximately minimizes interval score, described in Section <a href="#S6.SS1" title="6.1 Experimental settings ‣ 6 Simulated Residual Processes and Diagnostic Framework ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.1</span></a>. We divide the axis into 12 logarithmically spaced bins and compute the average within-bin standard deviation of the interval scores. A smaller average indicates tighter alignment across persistence configurations and hence a stronger collapse. We report the percentage reduction in scatter obtained by replacing <math id="S6.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S6.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
<table id="S6.E17" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.E17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100\left(1-\frac{S_{r}}{S_{\tau}}\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>τ</mi></msub></mfrac></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100\left(1-\frac{S_{r}}{S_{\tau}}\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(17)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S6.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{\tau}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>τ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{\tau}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the average within-bin standard deviation of interval scores when the horizontal axis is <math id="S6.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively. For the two families driven instead by an abrupt, deterministic change in the residual distribution — mean shift and variance shift — persistence is not the relevant axis. We therefore evaluate these settings using <em id="S6.p2.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">adaptation duration</em>, defined as the time required for coverage to recover following the shift.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S6.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 6 Simulated Residual Processes and Diagnostic Framework ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> summarizes the six families, the mechanism of non-exchangeability each represents, and the primary diagnostic applied to it.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.T2" class="ltx_table">

</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S6.T2.5.6" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S6.T2.5.6.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left">Variance shift</td>
<td id="S6.T2.5.6.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left">Abrupt, deterministic dispersion change</td>
<td id="S6.T2.5.6.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left">
<span id="S6.T2.5.6.3.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top">
<span id="S6.T2.5.6.3.1.1" class="ltx_p">Adaptation duration (first coverage-dip recovery) vs. <math id="S6.T2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> and calibration window <math id="S6.T2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math></span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S6.T2.5.7" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S6.T2.5.7.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb">Markov-switching</td>
<td id="S6.T2.5.7.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb">Stochastic, recurring regime change</td>
<td id="S6.T2.5.7.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb">
<span id="S6.T2.5.7.3.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top">
<span id="S6.T2.5.7.3.1.1" class="ltx_p">Curve collapse under <math id="S6.T2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\mathrm{regime}}=\tau/L_{\mathrm{regime}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>regime</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>regime</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\mathrm{regime}}=\tau/L_{\mathrm{regime}}</annotation></semantics></math>; regime-mismatch pathology when the target regime differs from the regime at construction</span>
</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<section id="S6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.1 </span>Experimental settings</h3>

<div id="S6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Unless stated otherwise, each simulation uses <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=7000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=7000</annotation></semantics></math> time steps, target miscoverage level <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0.1</annotation></semantics></math>, and 10 independent random seeds. We consider delays <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau\in\{1,\allowbreak 5,\allowbreak 10,\allowbreak 15,\allowbreak 20,\allowbreak 30,\allowbreak 40\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>40</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau\in\{1,\allowbreak 5,\allowbreak 10,\allowbreak 15,\allowbreak 20,\allowbreak 30,\allowbreak 40\}</annotation></semantics></math> and step sizes
<math id="S6.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma\in\{0.001,\allowbreak 0.002,\allowbreak 0.004,\allowbreak 0.008,\allowbreak 0.016,\allowbreak 0.032,\allowbreak 0.064,\allowbreak 0.128,\allowbreak 0.16\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0.001</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.002</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.004</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.008</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.016</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.032</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.064</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.128</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.16</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma\in\{0.001,\allowbreak 0.002,\allowbreak 0.004,\allowbreak 0.008,\allowbreak 0.016,\allowbreak 0.032,\allowbreak 0.064,\allowbreak 0.128,\allowbreak 0.16\}</annotation></semantics></math>. For select analyses, this grid is extended or refined with additional <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> values, or a longer simulation horizon to better resolve a specific pattern. Such extensions are visible in the corresponding figures. Any family-specific extensions to these grids are described in the corresponding subsection.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For each residual family and delay, we select the step size <math id="S6.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>γ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> using a coverage-aware rule based on the interval score, averaged over the <math id="S6.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> random seeds. When comparisons span multiple persistence values, shift magnitudes, calibration-window lengths, or normalization constructions, <math id="S6.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>γ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> is selected separately for each configuration. We first retain all step sizes whose average interval score is within <math id="S6.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the minimum over the candidate grid. Among these near-optimal values, we select the step size with the lowest interval score and empirical coverage of at least <math id="S6.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.89" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.89</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.89</annotation></semantics></math>, whenever such a candidate exists. If no near-optimal candidate satisfies this coverage threshold, we select the unrestricted interval-score minimizer. This rule favors solutions with approximately adequate coverage while avoiding a hard coverage constraint.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The calibration-window length <math id="S6.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> is chosen based on the residual distribution. For the Gaussian, AR(1), and GARCH(1,1) families, the unconditional distribution is stationary, so residuals from the distant past remain informative. We use <math id="S6.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=500" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>500</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=500</annotation></semantics></math> to reduce variability in the estimated conformal quantile. For the mean-shift and variance-shift families, pre-shift residuals may no longer represent the current distribution. For Markov-switching, a long window mixes residuals across regimes. In both cases, we use the shorter window <math id="S6.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=250" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>250</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=250</annotation></semantics></math> to limit contamination and provide an additional source of adaptation alongside <math id="S6.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">All reported results are averaged over the 10 seeds. Unless noted otherwise, the same simulation settings and evaluation procedure are used across residual families.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.2 </span>Gaussian — exchangeable baseline</h3>

<div id="S6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We first consider independent Gaussian residuals,</p>
<table id="S6.E18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.E18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon_{t}\overset{\mathrm{i.i.d.}}{\sim}\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^{2})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>ε</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mrow><mi mathsize="0.700em">i</mi><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="0.700em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mi mathsize="0.700em">i</mi><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="0.700em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mi mathsize="0.700em">d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="0.700em">.</mo></mrow></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon_{t}\overset{\mathrm{i.i.d.}}{\sim}\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^{2}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(18)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">with <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu=0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma=1</annotation></semantics></math>. This setting satisfies the exchangeability assumption and therefore
serves as the baseline against which the adaptive methods are evaluated. It represents a stable, well-specified forecasting setting in which the residual variation consists solely of independent, irreducible noise.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.3 </span>AR(1) — temporal dependence</h3>

<div id="S6.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To study the effect of serial dependence, we generate residuals from the stationary AR(1) process</p>
<table id="S6.E19" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.E19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon_{t+1}=\varphi\varepsilon_{t}+\eta_{t+1},\qquad\eta_{t}\overset{\mathrm{i.i.d.}}{\sim}\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_{\eta}^{2})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>ε</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>φ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ε</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>η</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mrow><mi mathsize="0.700em">i</mi><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="0.700em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mi mathsize="0.700em">i</mi><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="0.700em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mi mathsize="0.700em">d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="0.700em">.</mo></mrow></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>η</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon_{t+1}=\varphi\varepsilon_{t}+\eta_{t+1},\qquad\eta_{t}\overset{\mathrm{i.i.d.}}{\sim}\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_{\eta}^{2}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(19)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Such dependence may arise when the forecasting model fails to capture a persistent component of the data-generating process, such as a slowly varying trend or a seasonal pattern. The omitted structure may then be inherited by the residual sequence. For a stationary AR(1) process, the lag-<math id="S6.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> autocorrelation is</p>
<table id="S6.Ex17" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.Ex17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(k)=\operatorname{Corr}(\varepsilon_{t},\varepsilon_{t+k})=\varphi^{k}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Corr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ε</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ε</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>φ</mi><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho(k)=\operatorname{Corr}(\varepsilon_{t},\varepsilon_{t+k})=\varphi^{k}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Writing <math id="S6.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\varphi^{k}=e^{-k/L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>φ</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mi>k</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>e</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varphi^{k}=e^{-k/L}</annotation></semantics></math> defines the memory length <math id="S6.SS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="L:=-1/\log\varphi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo rspace="0em">:=</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>log</mi><mi>φ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L:=-1/\log\varphi</annotation></semantics></math>, at which the autocorrelation has decayed to <math id="S6.SS3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> of its lag-zero value. We characterize the feedback delay relative to this intrinsic time scale using the delay-to-memory ratio <math id="S6.SS3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S6.E20" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.E20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon}:=\frac{\tau}{L},\qquad L:=-\frac{1}{\log\varphi}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>ε</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mfrac><mi>τ</mi><mi>L</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>φ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon}:=\frac{\tau}{L},\qquad L:=-\frac{1}{\log\varphi}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(20)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The autocorrelation remaining across the delay is then <math id="S6.SS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(\tau)=e^{-r_{\varepsilon}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>ε</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho(\tau)=e^{-r_{\varepsilon}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus, when <math id="S6.SS3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon}\ll 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>ε</mi></msub><mo>≪</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon}\ll 1</annotation></semantics></math>, substantial dependence remains between the residuals available for calibration and the residual to be covered. When <math id="S6.SS3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon}\gg 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>ε</mi></msub><mo>≫</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon}\gg 1</annotation></semantics></math>, this dependence has largely dissipated before feedback becomes available.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS3.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS3.p5.1" class="ltx_p">We vary <math id="S6.SS3.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varphi\in\{0.1,\allowbreak 0.6,\allowbreak 0.85,\allowbreak 0.95,\allowbreak 0.99\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>φ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0.1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.85</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.95</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.99</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varphi\in\{0.1,\allowbreak 0.6,\allowbreak 0.85,\allowbreak 0.95,\allowbreak 0.99\}</annotation></semantics></math>, corresponding to memory lengths <math id="S6.SS3.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L\approx\{0.43,\allowbreak 1.96,\allowbreak 6.15,\allowbreak 19.50,\allowbreak 99.50\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0.43</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1.96</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6.15</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>19.50</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99.50</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L\approx\{0.43,\allowbreak 1.96,\allowbreak 6.15,\allowbreak 19.50,\allowbreak 99.50\}</annotation></semantics></math> steps. The resulting configurations span delay-to-memory ratios <math id="S6.SS3.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> ranging from approximately <math id="S6.SS3.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.01" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.01</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.01</annotation></semantics></math>, for <math id="S6.SS3.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varphi=0.99" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>φ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.99</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varphi=0.99</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.SS3.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=1</annotation></semantics></math>, to approximately <math id="S6.SS3.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="92" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>92</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">92</annotation></semantics></math>, for <math id="S6.SS3.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varphi=0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>φ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varphi=0.1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.SS3.p5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=40" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=40</annotation></semantics></math>. The grid therefore includes regimes in which the delay is much shorter than, comparable to, and much longer than the dependence time scale.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS3.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS3.p6.1" class="ltx_p">To isolate the effect of persistence from changes in unconditional variance, we set the innovation standard deviation to <math id="S6.SS3.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{\eta}=\sqrt{1-\varphi^{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>η</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>φ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{\eta}=\sqrt{1-\varphi^{2}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Equivalently, the one-step conditional variance is <math id="S6.SS3.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_{t+1}\mid\varepsilon_{t})=\sigma_{\eta}^{2}=1-\varphi^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Var</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ε</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>ε</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>η</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>φ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_{t+1}\mid\varepsilon_{t})=\sigma_{\eta}^{2}=1-\varphi^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. Under stationarity, this choice fixes the unconditional variance at <math id="S6.SS3.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_{t})=\sigma_{\eta}^{2}/(1-\varphi^{2})=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Var</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ε</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>η</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>φ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_{t})=\sigma_{\eta}^{2}/(1-\varphi^{2})=1</annotation></semantics></math> for every value of <math id="S6.SS3.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varphi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>φ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varphi</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.4 </span>GARCH(1,1) — volatility clustering</h3>

<div id="S6.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To study time variation in residual scale, we generate residuals from a GARCH(1,1) process,</p>
<table id="S6.E21" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.E21.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\varepsilon_{t}=\sigma_{t}\eta_{t},\qquad\sigma_{t}^{2}=\omega+\alpha\varepsilon_{t-1}^{2}+\beta\sigma_{t-1}^{2},\qquad\eta_{t}\overset{\mathrm{i.i.d.}}{\sim}\mathcal{N}(0,1)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ε</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mi>ω</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>α</mi><msubsup><mi>ε</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mover accent="true"><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mrow><mi mathsize="0.700em">i</mi><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="0.700em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mi mathsize="0.700em">i</mi><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="0.700em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mi mathsize="0.700em">d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="0.700em">.</mo></mrow></mover><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon_{t}=\sigma_{t}\eta_{t},\qquad\sigma_{t}^{2}=\omega+\alpha\varepsilon_{t-1}^{2}+\beta\sigma_{t-1}^{2},\qquad\eta_{t}\overset{\mathrm{i.i.d.}}{\sim}\mathcal{N}(0,1).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(21)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SS4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">This process produces volatility clustering: large residuals tend to be followed by residuals of large magnitude, although their signs remain unpredictable. Such behavior may arise when the difficulty of the forecasting problem varies over time and persists across consecutive periods.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The distinction from the AR(1) setting concerns the feature of the residual distribution that is predictable. In the AR(1) process, dependence appears in the conditional mean of the residual. In the GARCH process, the conditional mean remains zero, while the conditional variance <math id="S6.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{t}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{t}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> evolves over time. Consequently, temporal information is relevant primarily for adapting the width of the prediction interval rather than its location.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The squared residuals of a GARCH(1,1) process admit an ARMA(1,1) representation. Let <math id="S6.SS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu_{t}:=\varepsilon_{t}^{2}-\sigma_{t}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ν</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>ε</mi><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu_{t}:=\varepsilon_{t}^{2}-\sigma_{t}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the volatility innovation, which has
conditional mean zero. Substituting <math id="S6.SS4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{t}^{2}=\varepsilon_{t}^{2}-\nu_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>ε</mi><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>ν</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{t}^{2}=\varepsilon_{t}^{2}-\nu_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> into (<a href="#S6.E21" title="In 6.4 GARCH(1,1) — volatility clustering ‣ 6 Simulated Residual Processes and Diagnostic Framework ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">21</span></a>) gives</p>
<table id="S6.E22" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.E22.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon_{t}^{2}=\omega+(\alpha+\beta)\varepsilon_{t-1}^{2}+\nu_{t}-\beta\nu_{t-1}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>ε</mi><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ω</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>ε</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>ν</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ν</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon_{t}^{2}=\omega+(\alpha+\beta)\varepsilon_{t-1}^{2}+\nu_{t}-\beta\nu_{t-1}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(22)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SS4.p3.2" class="ltx_p">Thus, the dependence in the squared residuals decays geometrically at a rate governed by <math id="S6.SS4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha+\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha+\beta</annotation></semantics></math>. We therefore define the volatility memory length and the corresponding delay-to-memory ratio as</p>
<table id="S6.E23" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.E23.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon^{2}}:=\frac{\tau}{L_{\mathrm{vol}}}\qquad L_{\mathrm{vol}}:=\frac{-1}{\log(\alpha+\beta)}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><msup><mi>ε</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msub><mo>:=</mo><mfrac><mi>τ</mi><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>vol</mi></msub></mfrac></mrow><mspace style="width:2em;" width="2em"></mspace><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>vol</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon^{2}}:=\frac{\tau}{L_{\mathrm{vol}}}\qquad L_{\mathrm{vol}}:=\frac{-1}{\log(\alpha+\beta)}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(23)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS4.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS4.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Unlike <math id="S6.SS4.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> in the AR(1) setting, <math id="S6.SS4.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{\mathrm{vol}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>vol</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{\mathrm{vol}}</annotation></semantics></math> measures persistence in residual magnitude rather than in the residual values themselves. We vary <math id="S6.SS4.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha+\beta\in\{0.5,\allowbreak 0.9,\allowbreak 0.95,\allowbreak 0.99\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.9</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.95</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.99</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha+\beta\in\{0.5,\allowbreak 0.9,\allowbreak 0.95,\allowbreak 0.99\}</annotation></semantics></math>, corresponding to volatility memory lengths <math id="S6.SS4.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{\mathrm{vol}}\approx\{1.44,\allowbreak 9.49,\allowbreak 19.50,\allowbreak 99.50\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>vol</mi></msub><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1.44</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9.49</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>19.50</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99.50</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{\mathrm{vol}}\approx\{1.44,\allowbreak 9.49,\allowbreak 19.50,\allowbreak 99.50\}</annotation></semantics></math> steps. We fix <math id="S6.SS4.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0.1</annotation></semantics></math> and set <math id="S6.SS4.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta=(\alpha+\beta)-0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta=(\alpha+\beta)-0.1</annotation></semantics></math>, so that persistence varies through a single parameter. To fix the unconditional variance across configurations, we set <math id="S6.SS4.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega=1-\alpha-\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ω</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega=1-\alpha-\beta</annotation></semantics></math>. Under stationarity, <math id="S6.SS4.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_{t})=\omega/(1-\alpha-\beta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Var</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ε</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ω</mi><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_{t})=\omega/(1-\alpha-\beta)</annotation></semantics></math>, so this choice yields <math id="S6.SS4.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_{t})=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Var</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ε</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_{t})=1</annotation></semantics></math> for every persistence level.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS4.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS4.p5.1" class="ltx_p">A common refinement is to normalize residuals by an estimate of their conditional scale before forming <math id="S6.SS4.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, and then rescale the resulting quantiles when constructing the prediction interval. This can reduce heteroskedasticity in the residuals and make their distribution more stable over time <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gibbs and Candès, 2021</a>)</cite>. The GARCH family provides a natural setting for evaluating this construction because, unlike the Gaussian and AR(1) families, its conditional variance evolves over time. In this setting, normalization can reduce the effect of volatility clustering by expressing each residual relative to its conditional standard deviation. However, with delayed forecasting, an additional issue arises: the conditional scale at the time the interval is constructed may differ from the scale at the target time <math id="S6.SS4.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t+\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t+\tau</annotation></semantics></math>. To separate these two effects, we compare the unnormalized construction with two oracle normalization methods, summarized in Table <a href="#S6.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 6.4 GARCH(1,1) — volatility clustering ‣ 6 Simulated Residual Processes and Diagnostic Framework ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>. The <em id="S6.SS4.p5.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">current-scale oracle</em> uses the true conditional standard deviation <math id="S6.SS4.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> both to normalize the residual and to rescale the target interval. The <em id="S6.SS4.p5.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">target-scale oracle</em> also normalizes using <math id="S6.SS4.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, but rescales the interval using the realized target-time scale <math id="S6.SS4.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{t+\tau}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{t+\tau}</annotation></semantics></math>. The target-scale oracle is included specifically as a diagnostic to isolate whether deterioration in the current-scale oracle is caused by the delay-induced mismatch between the scale at interval construction and the scale realized at the target time, rather than by normalization itself. Because both methods rely on knowledge of the true conditional scale, they are non-deployable and are used only for diagnostic purposes.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS4.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS4.p6.1" class="ltx_p">To examine the normalization behavior once the feedback delay approaches and exceeds the volatility memory length, we additionally evaluate the most persistent configuration, <math id="S6.SS4.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha+\beta=0.99" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0.99</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha+\beta=0.99</annotation></semantics></math>, at <math id="S6.SS4.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau\in\{100,300\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>100,300</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau\in\{100,300\}</annotation></semantics></math>, corresponding to <math id="S6.SS4.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon^{2}}\approx 1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><msup><mi>ε</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msub><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon^{2}}\approx 1.0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.SS4.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon^{2}}\approx 3.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><msup><mi>ε</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msub><mo>≈</mo><mn>3.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon^{2}}\approx 3.0</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively. These extended-delay runs are used only for the normalization diagnostic and use a longer simulation horizon of <math id="S6.SS4.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=12{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12,000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=12{,}000</annotation></semantics></math>.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.T3" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S6.T3.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 3</span>: </span><span id="S6.T3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Scale information used by the GARCH normalization experiments.</span></figcaption>
