</section>
<section id="S6.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.5 </span>Mean and Variance Shift — Abrupt Changes in Residual Location and Scale</h3>

<div id="S6.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To study adaptation to abrupt changes in the residual distribution, we generate piecewise Gaussian residuals over three <math id="S6.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="800" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>800</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">800</annotation></semantics></math>-step segments: a baseline period, a shifted period, and a return to baseline. This setup captures both adaptation after the onset of a shift and recovery once the residual distribution returns to its initial state. Each shift magnitude or ratio is simulated separately, so the response to one shift does not affect the evaluation of another. The segment length is sufficient for the calibration window to discard pre-transition residuals and for post-transition behavior to be observed beyond the longest delay considered.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We use a primary calibration window of <math id="S6.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=250" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>250</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=250</annotation></semantics></math>. Unlike the stationary Gaussian, AR(1), and GARCH(1,1) settings, observations from before a change point may no longer be representative of the current residual distribution. A shorter window therefore provides an additional source of adaptation by removing all pre-transition residuals within <math id="S6.SS5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> steps. To examine whether faster turnover improves adaptation under repeated changes, we also repeat each combined-shift trajectory below with <math id="S6.SS5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=100</annotation></semantics></math>, holding all other settings fixed.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We measure <em id="S6.SS5.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">adaptation speed</em> by the duration of the first coverage dip following each shift, defined as the number of steps between the first time rolling empirical coverage, computed over a <math id="S6.SS5.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math>-observation window, falls below <math id="S6.SS5.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.89" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.89</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.89</annotation></semantics></math> and the first subsequent time it returns to at least <math id="S6.SS5.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.89" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.89</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.89</annotation></semantics></math>. Only the first dip is considered. If coverage does not recover before the segment ends, the duration is recorded at the segment boundary and treated as right-censored. We compute this measure for each combination of shift magnitude and <math id="S6.SS5.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> using the corresponding <math id="S6.SS5.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>γ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math>, selected separately for <math id="S6.SS5.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=250" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>250</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=250</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.SS5.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=100</annotation></semantics></math>.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<section id="S6.SS5.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Mean shift:</h4>

<div id="S6.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We hold the standard deviation fixed at <math id="S6.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma=1</annotation></semantics></math> and shift the mean,</p>
<table id="S6.E24" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.E24.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu(t)=\begin{cases}0,&amp;0\leq t&lt;800,\\
\Delta,&amp;800\leq t&lt;1600,\\
0,&amp;1600\leq t&lt;2400,\end{cases}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>800</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mn>800</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1600</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mn>1600</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>2400</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu(t)=\begin{cases}0,&amp;0\leq t&lt;800,\\
\Delta,&amp;800\leq t&lt;1600,\\
0,&amp;1600\leq t&lt;2400,\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(24)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">with <math id="S6.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\in\{0.5,\allowbreak 1,\allowbreak 2,\allowbreak 4\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\in\{0.5,\allowbreak 1,\allowbreak 2,\allowbreak 4\}</annotation></semantics></math>, ranging from shifts small relative to the nominal Gaussian interval half-width, <math id="S6.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{0.95}\sigma\approx 1.645" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>0.95</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.645</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{0.95}\sigma\approx 1.645</annotation></semantics></math>, to shifts that substantially exceed it. To examine tracking under repeated shifts, we construct a combined-shift trajectory alternating baseline and each magnitude, <math id="S6.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\,0,\Delta_{1},0,\Delta_{2},0,\Delta_{3},0,\Delta_{4},0\,]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn> 0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[\,0,\Delta_{1},0,\Delta_{2},0,\Delta_{3},0,\Delta_{4},0\,]</annotation></semantics></math>, with <math id="S6.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="800" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>800</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">800</annotation></semantics></math>-step segments and total horizon <math id="S6.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=7200" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7200</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=7200</annotation></semantics></math>.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS5.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Variance shift:</h4>

<div id="S6.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We hold the mean fixed at <math id="S6.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu=0</annotation></semantics></math> and shift the standard deviation by a post-to-pre ratio <math id="S6.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=\sigma_{\mathrm{post}}/\sigma_{\mathrm{pre}}\in\{1.5,\allowbreak 2,\allowbreak 3,\allowbreak 5,\allowbreak 8\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>post</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>pre</mi></msub></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=\sigma_{\mathrm{post}}/\sigma_{\mathrm{pre}}\in\{1.5,\allowbreak 2,\allowbreak 3,\allowbreak 5,\allowbreak 8\}</annotation></semantics></math>. Unlike an extreme mean shift, a large increase in scale does not force a miss at every time point, since the residual distribution remains centered at zero. The combined-shift trajectory alternates baseline and each ratio, <math id="S6.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\,1,r_{1},1,r_{2},1,r_{3},1,r_{4},1,r_{5},1\,]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn> 1</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[\,1,r_{1},1,r_{2},1,r_{3},1,r_{4},1,r_{5},1\,]</annotation></semantics></math>, with <math id="S6.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="800" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>800</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">800</annotation></semantics></math>-step segments and total horizon <math id="S6.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=8800" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8800</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=8800</annotation></semantics></math>.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.6 </span>Markov-switching — stochastic and recurring regime changes</h3>

<div id="S6.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To study recurring changes in the residual distribution, we generate residuals from a
two-state hidden Markov model <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hamilton, 1994</a>; <a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zucchini and MacDonald, 2009</a>)</cite>. Let
<math id="S6.SS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t}\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t}\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the latent regime at time <math id="S6.SS6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, with transition matrix</p>
<table id="S6.Ex18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.Ex18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P=\begin{pmatrix}p_{00}&amp;1-p_{00}\\
1-p_{11}&amp;p_{11}\end{pmatrix},\qquad P_{ij}=\Pr(A_{t}=j\mid A_{t-1}=i)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>00</mn></msub></mtd><mtd><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>00</mn></msub></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>11</mn></msub></mrow></mtd><mtd><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>11</mn></msub></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P=\begin{pmatrix}p_{00}&amp;1-p_{00}\\
1-p_{11}&amp;p_{11}\end{pmatrix},\qquad P_{ij}=\Pr(A_{t}=j\mid A_{t-1}=i).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SS6.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Conditional on the active regime, the residual is generated according to</p>
<table id="S6.E25" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.E25.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon_{t}\mid A_{t}=j\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu_{j},\sigma_{j}^{2})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>ε</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>j</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon_{t}\mid A_{t}=j\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu_{j},\sigma_{j}^{2}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(25)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SS6.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Conditional on the state sequence, the residual draws are independent over time.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The chain has stationary distribution <math id="S6.SS6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi=(\pi_{0},\pi_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi=(\pi_{0},\pi_{1})</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S6.SS6.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the
long-run marginal probability of occupying state <math id="S6.SS6.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>. The stationary distribution satisfies <math id="S6.SS6.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi P=\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi P=\pi</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.SS6.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{0}+\pi_{1}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{0}+\pi_{1}=1</annotation></semantics></math>. Solving these
conditions gives</p>
<table id="S6.Ex19" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.Ex19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{0}=\frac{1-p_{11}}{2-p_{00}-p_{11}},\qquad\pi_{1}=\frac{1-p_{00}}{2-p_{00}-p_{11}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>11</mn></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>00</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>11</mn></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>00</mn></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>00</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>11</mn></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{0}=\frac{1-p_{11}}{2-p_{00}-p_{11}},\qquad\pi_{1}=\frac{1-p_{00}}{2-p_{00}-p_{11}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SS6.p2.2" class="ltx_p">In the simulations, the latent chain is initialized in state <math id="S6.SS6.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>. We generate and
discard 200 burn-in observations before retaining the <math id="S6.SS6.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> observations used in the
experiment. This burn-in reduces the influence of the fixed initial state and allows
the state distribution to approach <math id="S6.SS6.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> before evaluation begins.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Unlike the deterministic mean- and variance-shift families, regime changes in the Markov-switching setting occur randomly and repeatedly. The construction represents an environment that alternates between operating conditions that tend to remain active for multiple consecutive time steps, such as baseline and shifted periods or calm and volatile periods. This distinction is particularly relevant under delayed feedback. An interval issued at time <math id="S6.SS6.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> for target time <math id="S6.SS6.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t+\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t+\tau</annotation></semantics></math> is constructed using information available at or before time <math id="S6.SS6.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, but the target residual is generated under state <math id="S6.SS6.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t+\tau}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t+\tau}</annotation></semantics></math>, which may differ from the state at construction.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS6.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS6.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SS6.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Delay-to-memory ratio:</span>
For the two-state transition matrix above, the unique non-unit eigenvalue is
<math id="S6.SS6.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{2}=p_{00}+p_{11}-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>00</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>11</mn></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{2}=p_{00}+p_{11}-1</annotation></semantics></math>. Appendix <a href="#A2.SS1" title="B.1 Autocorrelation of the two-state regime indicator ‣ Appendix B Autocorrelation Structure of the Markov-Switching Process ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.1</span></a> derives the corresponding
lag-<math id="S6.SS6.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> state autocorrelation,</p>
<table id="S6.E26" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.E26.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{Corr}(A_{t},A_{t+k})=\lambda_{2}^{k},\qquad k\geq 0." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Corr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mn>2</mn><mi>k</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{Corr}(A_{t},A_{t+k})=\lambda_{2}^{k},\qquad k\geq 0.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(26)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SS6.p4.2" class="ltx_p">Here, persistence refers specifically to the rate at which information about the
current latent state is lost across time. A larger positive value of <math id="S6.SS6.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>λ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>
corresponds to slower decay and hence greater persistence. All transition matrices used
in the experiments satisfy <math id="S6.SS6.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0&lt;\lambda_{2}&lt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0&lt;\lambda_{2}&lt;1</annotation></semantics></math>, so the state autocorrelation decays
monotonically with the lag.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS6.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS6.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Following the same convention used for the AR(1) and GARCH(1,1) families, we define the
regime memory length and delay-to-memory ratio as</p>
<table id="S6.E27" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.E27.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\mathrm{regime}}:=\frac{\tau}{L_{\mathrm{regime}}}\qquad L_{\mathrm{regime}}:=\frac{-1}{\log|\lambda_{2}|}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>regime</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mfrac><mi>τ</mi><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>regime</mi></msub></mfrac></mrow><mspace style="width:2em;" width="2em"></mspace><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>regime</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\mathrm{regime}}:=\frac{\tau}{L_{\mathrm{regime}}}\qquad L_{\mathrm{regime}}:=\frac{-1}{\log|\lambda_{2}|}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(27)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS6.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS6.p6.1" class="ltx_p">The latent-state dependence remaining
across the delay is therefore
<math id="S6.SS6.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\lambda_{2}|^{\tau}=e^{-r_{\mathrm{regime}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mi>τ</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>regime</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\lambda_{2}|^{\tau}=e^{-r_{\mathrm{regime}}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus,
<math id="S6.SS6.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\mathrm{regime}}\ll 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>regime</mi></msub><mo>≪</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\mathrm{regime}}\ll 1</annotation></semantics></math> indicates that substantial dependence remains between the
states at interval construction and at the target time, whereas
<math id="S6.SS6.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\mathrm{regime}}\gg 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>regime</mi></msub><mo>≫</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\mathrm{regime}}\gg 1</annotation></semantics></math> indicates that the chain has largely forgotten its earlier
state.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS6.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS6.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SS6.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Markov-switching regimes:</span>
We consider three state-dependent residual constructions:</p>
<table id="S6.E28" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.E28.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\begin{array}[]{lll}\text{Mean switching:}&amp;\mu_{0}=0,\quad\mu_{1}=\Delta,&amp;\sigma_{0}=\sigma_{1}=1,\\[5.69054pt]
\text{Variance switching:}&amp;\mu_{0}=\mu_{1}=0,&amp;\sigma_{0}=1,\quad\sigma_{1}=r,\\[5.69054pt]
\text{Joint switching:}&amp;\mu_{0}=0,\quad\mu_{1}=\Delta,&amp;\sigma_{0}=1,\quad\sigma_{1}=r.\end{array}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" columnalign="left"><mrow><mi>μ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mi>μ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mtext>Variance switching:</mtext></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mi>σ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mi>σ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mtext>Joint switching:</mtext></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mi>μ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mi>μ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left"
