switching:}&amp;\mu_{0}=0,\quad\mu_{1}=\Delta,&amp;\sigma_{0}=\sigma_{1}=1,\\[5.69054pt]
\text{Variance switching:}&amp;\mu_{0}=\mu_{1}=0,&amp;\sigma_{0}=1,\quad\sigma_{1}=r,\\[5.69054pt]
\text{Joint switching:}&amp;\mu_{0}=0,\quad\mu_{1}=\Delta,&amp;\sigma_{0}=1,\quad\sigma_{1}=r.\end{array}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(28)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SS6.p7.2" class="ltx_p">We fix <math id="S6.SS6.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta=4</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.SS6.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=5</annotation></semantics></math>.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS6.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS6.p8.1" class="ltx_p">Appendix <a href="#A2.SS2" title="B.2 Autocorrelation of state-dependent residual features ‣ Appendix B Autocorrelation Structure of the Markov-Switching Process ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.2</span></a> derives how latent-state persistence appears in the observed residuals and their transformations. Under mean and joint switching, the residual level inherits the geometric decay factor <math id="S6.SS6.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{2}^{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mn>2</mn><mi>k</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{2}^{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, although its autocorrelation magnitude is attenuated relative to the latent-state autocorrelation by within-state randomness. Under variance switching, the signed residual has zero autocorrelation because its conditional mean is zero in both states; the regime dependence instead appears in <math id="S6.SS6.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\varepsilon_{t}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>ε</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\varepsilon_{t}|</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.SS6.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon_{t}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>ε</mi><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon_{t}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus, across the three switching families, the relevant memory length remains <math id="S6.SS6.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{\mathrm{regime}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>regime</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{\mathrm{regime}}</annotation></semantics></math>, determined by the latent state process rather than by the attenuation in any particular observed feature. The corresponding positive-lag autocorrelation expressions are summarized in Table <a href="#A2.T8" title="Table 8 ‣ Step 6: Joint-switching residuals ‣ B.2 Autocorrelation of state-dependent residual features ‣ Appendix B Autocorrelation Structure of the Markov-Switching Process ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> in Appendix <a href="#A2.SS2" title="B.2 Autocorrelation of state-dependent residual features ‣ Appendix B Autocorrelation Structure of the Markov-Switching Process ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.2</span></a>.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS6.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS6.p9.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SS6.p9.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Symmetric transitions:</span>
For the primary experiment, we use symmetric transition matrices,</p>
<table id="S6.E29" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.E29.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P(p)=\begin{pmatrix}p&amp;1-p\\
1-p&amp;p\end{pmatrix},\qquad p\in\{0.80,0.90,0.95,0.97,0.99\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mi>p</mi></mtd><mtd><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></mtd><mtd><mi>p</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0.80</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.90</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.95</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.99</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(p)=\begin{pmatrix}p&amp;1-p\\
1-p&amp;p\end{pmatrix},\qquad p\in\{0.80,0.90,0.95,0.97,0.99\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(29)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SS6.p9.2" class="ltx_p">Symmetry fixes <math id="S6.SS6.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{0}=\pi_{1}=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{0}=\pi_{1}=0.5</annotation></semantics></math>, so the memory of the state process can be varied without changing the long-run frequency of either regime. Since <math id="S6.SS6.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{0},\mu_{1},\sigma_{0},\sigma_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{0},\mu_{1},\sigma_{0},\sigma_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> are held fixed across the grid, this also fixes the marginal residual distribution across persistence levels, isolating the effect of regime memory within each switching family. The corresponding non-unit eigenvalues are <math id="S6.SS6.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{2}=2p-1\in\{0.60,0.80,0.90,0.94,0.98\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0.60</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.80</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.90</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.94</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.98</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{2}=2p-1\in\{0.60,0.80,0.90,0.94,0.98\}</annotation></semantics></math>, giving memory lengths
<math id="S6.SS6.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{\mathrm{regime}}\approx\{1.96,4.48,9.49,16.16,49.50\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>regime</mi></msub><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1.96</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4.48</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9.49</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>16.16</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>49.50</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{\mathrm{regime}}\approx\{1.96,4.48,9.49,16.16,49.50\}</annotation></semantics></math>, ranging from frequent switching to long regime episodes. The memory length <math id="S6.SS6.p9.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{\mathrm{regime}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>regime</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{\mathrm{regime}}</annotation></semantics></math>, which governs autocorrelation decay, is distinct from the mean dwell time in a regime. The dwell time, <math id="S6.SS6.p9.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{\mathrm{dwell}}=1/(1-p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>dwell</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{\mathrm{dwell}}=1/(1-p)</annotation></semantics></math>, describes the expected duration of one uninterrupted regime episode. The corresponding dwell times are <math id="S6.SS6.p9.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{\mathrm{dwell}}\in\{5,10,20,33.3,100\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>dwell</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>33.3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{\mathrm{dwell}}\in\{5,10,20,33.3,100\}</annotation></semantics></math> across the same grid.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS6.p10" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS6.p10.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SS6.p10.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Normalization:</span>
We apply the same two normalization constructions used in the GARCH experiments (Table <a href="#S6.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 6.4 GARCH(1,1) — volatility clustering ‣ 6 Simulated Residual Processes and Diagnostic Framework ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>), replacing the conditional scales <math id="S6.SS6.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.SS6.p10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{t+\tau}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{t+\tau}</annotation></semantics></math> with the state-dependent scales <math id="S6.SS6.p10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{A_{t}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{A_{t}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.SS6.p10.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{A_{t+\tau}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{A_{t+\tau}}</annotation></semantics></math>. The current-state oracle uses <math id="S6.SS6.p10.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{A_{t}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{A_{t}}</annotation></semantics></math> for both residual normalization and target-interval scaling. The target-state oracle also normalizes by <math id="S6.SS6.p10.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{A_{t}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{A_{t}}</annotation></semantics></math>, but rescales the interval using <math id="S6.SS6.p10.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{A_{t+\tau}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{A_{t+\tau}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Comparing the two isolates the effect of the delay-induced mismatch between the scale at interval construction and the scale at the target time, assuming perfect knowledge of the current state. We restrict this experiment to the variance- and joint-switching regimes.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS6.p11" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS6.p11.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SS6.p11.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Regime-transition diagnostic:</span>
To examine whether interval performance deteriorates when the target regime differs from the regime at interval construction, we compare interval scores according to whether the latent state changes across the forecast horizon, defining the mismatch indicator <math id="S6.SS6.p11.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="M_{t,\tau}:=\mathbf{1}\{A_{t}\neq A_{t+\tau}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>:=</mo><mn>𝟏</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>≠</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{t,\tau}:=\mathbf{1}\{A_{t}\neq A_{t+\tau}\}</annotation></semantics></math>. Because the interval depends on a rolling calibration window rather than solely on <math id="S6.SS6.p11.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, mismatch status is an explanatory diagnostic rather than a complete characterization of the information used to construct
the interval. Under stationarity,</p>
<table id="S6.E30" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.E30.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pr(M_{t,\tau}=1)=2\pi_{0}\pi_{1}\left(1-\lambda_{2}^{\tau}\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mn>2</mn><mi>τ</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pr(M_{t,\tau}=1)=2\pi_{0}\pi_{1}\left(1-\lambda_{2}^{\tau}\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(30)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SS6.p11.2" class="ltx_p">which for a symmetric chain reduces to <math id="S6.SS6.p11.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pr(M_{t,\tau}=1)=\tfrac{1}{2}(1-e^{-r_{\mathrm{regime}}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>regime</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pr(M_{t,\tau}=1)=\tfrac{1}{2}(1-e^{-r_{\mathrm{regime}}})</annotation></semantics></math>,
connecting the delay-to-memory ratio directly to the mismatch frequency.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>The Effect of Delay on ACI Across Residual Regimes</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We organize the results by residual family. Throughout, we attend to how the step-size interacts with delay and persistence jointly to shape coverage, efficiency, and local calibration.</p>
</div>
<section id="S7.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">7.1 </span>Gaussian — exchangeable baseline</h3>

<div id="S7.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S7.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 7.1 Gaussian — exchangeable baseline ‣ 7 The Effect of Delay on ACI Across Residual Regimes ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> confirms the known one-step-ahead result of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zaffran et al. (2022)</a></cite> in the <math id="S7.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>-delayed setting. Under exchangeable i.i.d. residuals, increasing <math id="S7.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> monotonically worsens the interval score, from approximately <math id="S7.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.15</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.15</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="S7.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma=0.001" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.001</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma=0.001</annotation></semantics></math> to roughly <math id="S7.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.43" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.43</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.43</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="S7.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma=0.128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma=0.128</annotation></semantics></math>. This amounts to a <math id="S7.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7\%</annotation></semantics></math> efficiency loss with no coverage benefit. The effect is invariant to the delay: every row of the heatmap is flat across all seven values of <math id="S7.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>. When residuals are exchangeable and contain no temporal dependence, past residuals provide no information about future residuals, so delaying their feedback neither improves nor worsens performance. Coverage failure, marked <math id="S7.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> in the figure, occurs only for <math id="S7.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma=0.128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma=0.128</annotation></semantics></math> and uniformly across all <math id="S7.SS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>, indicating that it is caused by an overly large step size rather than by delay. This panel therefore provides a baseline in which <math id="S7.SS1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>-DACI recovers classical ACI behavior when there is no temporal dependence for the delay to interact with.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<figure id="S7.F1" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2609.07251v1/figures/Delayed_ACI/gaussian_score_heatmap.png" id="S7.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:343/270;" width="343" height="270" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S7.F1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 1</span>: </span><span id="S7.F1.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Interval score heatmap for Gaussian (i.i.d.) residuals across the <math id="S7.F1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma\times\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma\times\tau</annotation></semantics></math> grid. Markers (<span id="S7.F1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">×</span>) indicate coverage below 0.89.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">7.2 </span>AR(1) — temporal dependence</h3>

<div id="S7.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S7.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 7.2 AR(1) — temporal dependence ‣ 7 The Effect of Delay on ACI Across Residual Regimes ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> reports the achieved interval score at the approximately score-minimizing step size <math id="S7.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>γ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math>, selected using the coverage-aware criterion described in Section <a href="#S6.SS1" title="6.1 Experimental settings ‣ 6 Simulated Residual Processes and Diagnostic Framework ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.1</span></a>. In the left panel, plotted against the delay <math id="S7.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>, each persistence level traces a distinct curve. Higher persistence is associated with lower scores at <math id="S7.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=1</annotation></semantics></math> and a steeper increase as the delay grows, indicating that performance depends jointly on <math id="S7.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varphi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>φ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varphi</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S7.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>. In the right panel, the score is plotted against the ratio <math id="S7.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon}=\tau/L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>ε</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon}=\tau/L</annotation></semantics></math>. This reparameterization produces a substantial collapse across persistence levels. Plotting against <math id="S7.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>ε</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon}</annotation></semantics></math> reduces within-bin scatter by approximately <math id="S7.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="79\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>79</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">79\%</annotation></semantics></math> relative to plotting against <math id="S7.SS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>. This suggests that <math id="S7.SS2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>ε</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon}</annotation></semantics></math> is a useful scaling variable for performance under delay, although some persistence-dependent variation remains.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The collapsed relationship shows a transition near <math id="S7.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon}\approx 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>ε</mi></msub><mo>≈</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon}\approx 1</annotation></semantics></math>. For <math id="S7.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon}\lesssim 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>ε</mi></msub><mo>≲</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon}\lesssim 1</annotation></semantics></math>, the score is generally below the Gaussian baseline. The method attains a lower score than under exchangeable residuals with the same marginal variance, which is consistent with the approximately score-minimizing step size exploiting dependence between the residuals available for calibration and the residual <math id="S7.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> steps ahead that the interval must cover. The advantage is largest at small <math id="S7.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>ε</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon}</annotation></semantics></math>; for example, at <math id="S7.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varphi=0.99" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>φ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.99</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varphi=0.99</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S7.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=1</annotation></semantics></math>, the score is approximately <math id="S7.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.3</annotation></semantics></math>, compared with a baseline near <math id="S7.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.15</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.15</annotation></semantics></math>. This advantage holds without a coverage cost at <math id="S7.SS2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varphi=0.95" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>φ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.95</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varphi=0.95</annotation></semantics></math>, where coverage remains close to the nominal target. At <math id="S7.SS2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varphi=0.99" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>φ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.99</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varphi=0.99</annotation></semantics></math>, coverage in the same region falls to <math id="S7.SS2.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.83" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.83</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.83</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S7.SS2.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.86" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.86</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.86</annotation></semantics></math>, indicating that at the highest persistence level, part of the efficiency gain comes at the cost of coverage. For <math id="S7.SS2.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon}\gtrsim 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>ε</mi></msub><mo>≳</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon}\gtrsim 1</annotation></semantics></math>, the score approaches or exceeds the baseline. This is consistent with the relevant dependence having largely decayed once the delay reaches the memory scale. Under weak persistence, the score levels off near the Gaussian baseline. Under strong persistence, particularly for <math id="S7.SS2.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varphi=0.95" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>φ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.95</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varphi=0.95</annotation></semantics></math>, it remains above the baseline. One possible explanation is that serial dependence reduces the effective number of independent observations in the calibration window.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<figure id="S7.F2" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2609.07251v1/figures/Delayed_ACI/ar_performance_collapse.png" id="S7.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/198;" width="476" height="198" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S7.F2.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 2</span>: </span><span id="S7.F2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Achieved interval score for AR(1) residuals at the selected step size <math id="S7.F2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>γ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math>, shown by persistence level as a function of the raw delay <math id="S7.F2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> (left) and the delay-to-memory ratio <math id="S7.F2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>ε</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon}</annotation></semantics></math> (right). The dashed black line shows the i.i.d. Gaussian reference at <math id="S7.F2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma=0.001" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.001</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma=0.001</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S7.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S7.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 7.2 AR(1) — temporal dependence ‣ 7 The Effect of Delay on ACI Across Residual Regimes ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> reports the optimal step size <math id="S7.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>γ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math>. As with the achieved score, <math id="S7.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>γ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> is organized more clearly by the ratio <math id="S7.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>ε</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon}</annotation></semantics></math> than by <math id="S7.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> alone. In the left panel, its dependence on <math id="S7.SS2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> differs markedly across persistence levels, and the curves do not share a common transition. Against <math id="S7.SS2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>ε</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon}</annotation></semantics></math>, the behavior is more systematic. For <math id="S7.SS2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon}\ll 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>ε</mi></msub><mo>≪</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon}\ll 1</annotation></semantics></math>, large step sizes are optimal. As <math id="S7.SS2.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>ε</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon}</annotation></semantics></math> approaches one, <math id="S7.SS2.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>γ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> falls sharply, often reaching the lower boundary of the grid. This decline occurs near <math id="S7.SS2.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon}\approx 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>ε</mi></msub><mo>≈</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon}\approx 1</annotation></semantics></math>, where the achieved interval score also begins to level off, indicating a change in the optimal adaptation regime as the delay approaches the process memory length. When correlation survives the delay, a large step size allows the procedure to adapt to exploitable structure. Once that dependence has decayed, the residuals available for calibration carry little information about the target, and performance converges toward the exchangeable-residual case (Section <a href="#S7.SS1" title="7.1 Gaussian — exchangeable baseline ‣ 7 The Effect of Delay on ACI Across Residual Regimes ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7.1</span></a>), where increasing <math id="S7.SS2.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> monotonically worsens the interval score with no coverage benefit. This is consistent with the smallest step size minimizing the interval score once <math id="S7.SS2.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>ε</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon}</annotation></semantics></math> exceeds roughly one. Beyond the transition, however, <math id="S7.SS2.p3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>γ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> does not remain at the grid floor for the more persistent processes but returns to a slightly larger value. This reflects the coverage-aware selection rule: where the score-minimizing step size undercovers, the rule selects a larger step that restores coverage in most cases.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<figure id="S7.F3" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2609.07251v1/figures/Delayed_ACI/ar_collapse_comparison.png" id="S7.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/178;" width="476" height="178" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S7.F3.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 3</span>: </span><span id="S7.F3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Approximately score-minimizing step-size <math id="S7.F3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>γ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> for AR(1) residuals, against the delay <math id="S7.F3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> (left) and the delay-to-memory ratio <math id="S7.F3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>ε</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon}</annotation></semantics></math> (right).</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S7.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S7.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 7.2 AR(1) — temporal dependence ‣ 7 The Effect of Delay on ACI Across Residual Regimes ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> reports the interval score over the <math id="S7.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\gamma,\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\gamma,\tau)</annotation></semantics></math> grid for three persistence levels. Dots indicate mild undercoverage, <math id="S7.SS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.86\leq\mathrm{coverage}&lt;0.89" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.86</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>coverage</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.89</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.86\leq\mathrm{coverage}&lt;0.89</annotation></semantics></math>, while crosses indicate coverage below <math id="S7.SS2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.86" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.86</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.86</annotation></semantics></math>. The coverage-feasible region, consisting of unmarked cells, shrinks as <math id="S7.SS2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varphi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>φ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varphi</annotation></semantics></math> increases. For <math id="S7.SS2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varphi=0.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>φ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varphi=0.6</annotation></semantics></math>, undercoverage is concentrated at large step sizes and becomes substantial only at <math id="S7.SS2.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma=0.32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma=0.32</annotation></semantics></math>. For <math id="S7.SS2.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varphi=0.85" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>φ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.85</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varphi=0.85</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S7.SS2.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varphi=0.95" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>φ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.95</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varphi=0.95</annotation></semantics></math>, mild undercoverage advances from two directions: from large <math id="S7.SS2.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> throughout the grid and from small <math id="S7.SS2.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> at large <math id="S7.SS2.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>. These heatmap figures show why step-size selection should not rely on interval score alone. At higher persistence, the score-minimizing cells themselves undercover, though only mildly (marked by dots rather than crosses). Because undercoverage at the absolute minimum is mild, a coverage-compliant near-optimal step size is typically available, allowing coverage to be favored at little cost in efficiency. Substantial undercoverage, marked by crosses, occurs away from the score-minimizing region, where more aggressive updating worsens both calibration and interval score.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<figure id="S7.F4" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2609.07251v1/figures/Delayed_ACI/ar_score_heatmaps_selected_phi.png" id="S7.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/148;" width="476" height="148" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S7.F4.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 4</span>: </span><span id="S7.F4.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Interval score across the <math id="S7.F4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma\times\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma\times\tau</annotation></semantics></math> grid for AR(1) residuals at three persistence levels (<math id="S7.F4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varphi=0.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>φ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varphi=0.6</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S7.F4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.85" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.85</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.85</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S7.F4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.95" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.95</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.95</annotation></semantics></math>). A dot marks mild undercoverage (<math id="S7.F4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.86\leq\text{coverage}&lt;0.89" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.86</mn><mo>≤</mo><mtext>coverage</mtext><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.89</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.86\leq\text{coverage}&lt;0.89</annotation></semantics></math>) and a cross marks (<math id="S7.F4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{coverage}&lt;0.86" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>coverage</mtext><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.86</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{coverage}&lt;0.86</annotation></semantics></math>); unmarked cells meet coverage.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S7.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Local coverage error exhibits a different pattern from interval score. Although it generally increases as the delay grows relative to the memory length, the curves do not collapse across persistence levels, indicating that <math id="S7.SS2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>ε</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon}</annotation></semantics></math> alone does not explain differences in the magnitude of local calibration error. The full results are reported in Appendix <a href="#A3.SS1" title="C.1 AR(1) ‣ Appendix C Additional Results ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.1</span></a> (Figure <a href="#A3.F12" title="Figure 12 ‣ C.1 AR(1) ‣ Appendix C Additional Results ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a>).
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">7.3 </span>GARCH(1,1) — volatility clustering</h3>

<div id="S7.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S7.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 7.3 GARCH(1,1) — volatility clustering ‣ 7 The Effect of Delay on ACI Across Residual Regimes ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> reports the achieved interval
score for the unnormalized-residual construction at the optimal step size
<math id="S7.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>γ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math>, plotted against the delay <math id="S7.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> in the left panel and the
delay-to-memory ratio <math id="S7.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon^{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><msup><mi>ε</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon^{2}}</annotation></semantics></math> in the
right panel. In terms of the raw delay, the persistence regimes exhibit
distinct behavior. For <math id="S7.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha+\beta=0.99" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0.99</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha+\beta=0.99</annotation></semantics></math>, the interval score increases
from approximately <math id="S7.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.86" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3.86</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.86</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="S7.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=1</annotation></semantics></math>, below the i.i.d. Gaussian
baseline, to approximately <math id="S7.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.59" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.59</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.59</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="S7.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=40" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=40</annotation></semantics></math>, crossing the baseline
between <math id="S7.SS3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=5</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S7.SS3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=10</annotation></semantics></math>. The <math id="S7.SS3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha+\beta=0.95" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0.95</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha+\beta=0.95</annotation></semantics></math> curve shows a
similar but weaker deterioration, whereas the scores for
<math id="S7.SS3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha+\beta\in\{0.5,\allowbreak 0.9\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha+\beta\in\{0.5,\allowbreak 0.9\}</annotation></semantics></math> vary only mildly with <math id="S7.SS3.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> and
remain close to the Gaussian benchmark.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Reparameterizing the horizontal axis by <math id="S7.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon^{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><msup><mi>ε</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon^{2}}</annotation></semantics></math> improves the
alignment across persistence regimes, reducing the collapse metric by
approximately <math id="S7.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="46\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>46</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">46\%</annotation></semantics></math> relative to the raw-delay representation. The
improvement is nevertheless less pronounced than in the AR(1) setting,
where the corresponding reduction is approximately <math id="S7.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="79\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>79</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">79\%</annotation></semantics></math>. Moreover,
unlike the AR(1) curves, the GARCH(1,1) curves provide limited evidence of
a common change in behavior near <math id="S7.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon^{2}}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><msup><mi>ε</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon^{2}}=1</annotation></semantics></math>. A substantial
improvement over the i.i.d. Gaussian baseline is observed only for the
most persistent process, <math id="S7.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha+\beta=0.99" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0.99</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha+\beta=0.99</annotation></semantics></math>, at the shortest delay. At
the remaining delays and persistence levels, achieved performance is
generally close to or worse than the Gaussian baseline. The larger
gains observed under AR(1) may indicate that dependence in the signed
residuals is more directly exploitable by the adaptive procedure than
dependence confined to the conditional variance, although the present
experiments do not isolate this mechanism. Thus, the delay-to-memory ratio organizes
the variation across GARCH persistence levels more effectively than the
raw delay, but it does not identify a sharp threshold separating regimes
in which volatility dependence is and is not beneficial.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<figure id="S7.F5" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2609.07251v1/figures/Delayed_ACI/garch_normal_performance_collapse.png" id="S7.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/218;" width="476" height="218" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S7.F5.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 5</span>: </span><span id="S7.F5.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Achieved interval score at the selected step-size <math id="S7.F5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>γ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> for GARCH(1,1) residuals (unnormalized
construction), against the delay <math id="S7.F5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> (left) and the delay-to-memory
ratio <math id="S7.F5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon^{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><msup><mi>ε</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon^{2}}</annotation></semantics></math> (right), across
persistence levels.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S7.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S7.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ 7.3 GARCH(1,1) — volatility clustering ‣ 7 The Effect of Delay on ACI Across Residual Regimes ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> reports the ratio of the interval score obtained with normalized residuals to that obtained with unnormalized residuals as a function of <math id="S7.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon^{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><msup><mi>ε</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon^{2}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Ratios below one indicate that normalization improves interval performance, whereas ratios above one indicate that it worsens performance. For the current-scale oracle, replacing <math id="S7.SS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S7.SS3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon^{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><msup><mi>ε</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon^{2}}</annotation></semantics></math> in the curve-collapse diagnostic reduces the within-bin scatter by approximately <math id="S7.SS3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>50</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50\%</annotation></semantics></math>, indicating that the benefit of normalization is strongly related to the delay relative to the volatility memory length.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<figure id="S7.F6" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2609.07251v1/figures/Delayed_ACI/garch_normal_normalization_ratio_vs_r_with_oracle_extended.png" id="S7.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:405/265;" width="405" height="265" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S7.F6.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 6</span>: </span><span id="S7.F6.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Ratio of the interval score obtained with normalized residuals to that obtained with unnormalized residuals for the GARCH(1,1) process, shown by persistence level as a function of <math id="S7.F6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon^{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><msup><mi>ε</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon^{2}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Solid lines correspond to the current-scale oracle, while dash-dotted lines correspond to the target-scale oracle.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S7.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">For the current-scale oracle, normalization is generally beneficial when <math id="S7.SS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon^{2}}&lt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><msup><mi>ε</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon^{2}}&lt;1</annotation></semantics></math>, particularly for the more persistent processes, whereas its effect is negligible for <math id="S7.SS3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha+\beta=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha+\beta=0.5</annotation></semantics></math>. As the delay approaches and exceeds the volatility memory length, the score ratios rise toward or above one. The extended-delay results for <math id="S7.SS3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha+\beta=0.99" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0.99</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha+\beta=0.99</annotation></semantics></math> reinforce this pattern: normalization becomes disadvantageous near <math id="S7.SS3.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon^{2}}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><msup><mi>ε</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon^{2}}=1</annotation></semantics></math> and deteriorates further by <math id="S7.SS3.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon^{2}}\approx 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><msup><mi>ε</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msub><mo>≈</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon^{2}}\approx 3</annotation></semantics></math>. To assess whether this deterioration is driven by scale mismatch rather than by normalization itself, we use the target-scale oracle as a diagnostic. Its score ratios remain below one throughout the plotted range. The improvement is modest for the lower-persistence processes but becomes substantial for <math id="S7.SS3.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha+\beta=0.99" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0.99</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha+\beta=0.99</annotation></semantics></math>, where the ratio continues to decline over the extended-delay runs and reaches approximately <math id="S7.SS3.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.80" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.80</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.80</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="S7.SS3.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\varepsilon^{2}}\approx 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><msup><mi>ε</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msub><mo>≈</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\varepsilon^{2}}\approx 3</annotation></semantics></math>. The widening separation between the current-scale and target-scale oracle curves indicates that the deterioration at longer delays is largely attributable to using the prediction-time scale <math id="S7.SS3.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> to rescale an interval intended for time <math id="S7.SS3.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t+\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t+\tau</annotation></semantics></math>. As prediction-time scale information becomes less informative at longer delays, access to the realized target-time scale becomes increasingly valuable. Although this oracle information is unavailable in practice, the result suggests that more accurate forecasts of <math id="S7.SS3.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{t+\tau}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{t+\tau}</annotation></semantics></math> could recover part of this benefit.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS3.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS3.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Normalization also generally improves local coverage stability. Across most GARCH configurations, the current-scale oracle yields lower worst-case local coverage error than the unnormalized construction, including at delays where its interval-score advantage has disappeared. This suggests that the delay-induced scale mismatch affects interval efficiency more strongly than local coverage stability. Full results are reported in Appendix <a href="#A3.SS2" title="C.2 GARCH(1,1) ‣ Appendix C Additional Results ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.2</span></a> (Figure <a href="#A3.F13" title="Figure 13 ‣ C.2 GARCH(1,1) ‣ Appendix C Additional Results ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">7.4 </span>Mean and variance shifts</h3>

<div id="S7.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figures <a href="#S7.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ 7.4 Mean and variance shifts ‣ 7 The Effect of Delay on ACI Across Residual Regimes ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> and <a href="#S7.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ 7.4 Mean and variance shifts ‣ 7 The Effect of Delay on ACI Across Residual Regimes ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> show rolling coverage and width along the combined-shift trajectories described in Section <a href="#S6.SS5" title="6.5 Mean and Variance Shift — Abrupt Changes in Residual Location and Scale ‣ 6 Simulated Residual Processes and Diagnostic Framework ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.5</span></a>, in which successive regime changes increase in magnitude before returning to the baseline regime. Results are shown using the primary calibration-window length <math id="S7.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=250" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>250</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=250</annotation></semantics></math>. In both families, regime transitions produce localized coverage failures whose depth generally increases with shift magnitude and feedback delay. Longer delays produce more severe transient miscoverage, although their effect on the duration of these failures is less systematic. The corresponding width trajectories reveal an important structural difference between changes in residual location (mean shifts) and changes in residual scale (variance shifts). These qualitative coverage and width patterns remain visible when the rolling window is shortened from <math id="S7.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S7.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>20</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20</annotation></semantics></math> observations (Figures <a href="#A3.F14" title="Figure 14 ‣ C.3 Mean and Variance Shift ‣ Appendix C Additional Results ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a> and <a href="#A3.F15" title="Figure 15 ‣ C.3 Mean and Variance Shift ‣ Appendix C Additional Results ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a> in the appendix <a href="#A3.SS3" title="C.3 Mean and Variance Shift ‣ Appendix C Additional Results ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.3</span></a>). Mean shifts produce sharp width expansions followed by gradual contraction as the interval adapts to the new residual location. Variance shifts instead produce sustained, regime-specific width plateaus that increase with residual scale. During variance shifts, after the process returns to baseline, the temporarily oversized intervals generate overcoverage while width contracts. Thus, mean shifts produce transient width spikes at regime transitions, whereas variance shifts produce sustained, regime-specific width plateaus.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<figure id="S7.F7" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2609.07251v1/figures/Delayed_ACI/shift_combined_multishift__coverage_width_stacked_mean.png" id="S7.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/270;" width="476" height="270" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S7.F7.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 7</span>: </span><span id="S7.F7.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Rolling coverage (top) and interval width (bottom) along the combined mean-shift trajectory using calibration-window length <math id="S7.F7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=250" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>250</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=250</annotation></semantics></math>, computed over a window of <math id="S7.F7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math> observations.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="S7.F8" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2609.07251v1/figures/Delayed_ACI/shift_combined_multishift__coverage_width_stacked_variance.png" id="S7.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/270;" width="476" height="270" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S7.F8.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 8</span>: </span><span id="S7.F8.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Rolling coverage (top) and interval width (bottom) along the combined variance-shift trajectory using calibration-window length <math id="S7.F8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=250" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>250</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=250</annotation></semantics></math>, computed over a window of <math id="S7.F8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math> observations.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S7.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Although coverage troughs generally deepen with delay, adaptation duration is not monotonic in <math id="S7.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> for either shift family. For example, under <math id="S7.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=250" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>250</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=250</annotation></semantics></math>,
adaptation duration decreases from <math id="S7.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="131" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>131</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">131</annotation></semantics></math> steps at <math id="S7.SS4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=5</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S7.SS4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="114" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>114</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">114</annotation></semantics></math> steps at <math id="S7.SS4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=40" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=40</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S7.SS4.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta=4</annotation></semantics></math>, and from <math id="S7.SS4.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="165" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>165</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">165</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S7.SS4.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="143" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>143</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">143</annotation></semantics></math> steps for <math id="S7.SS4.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=8</annotation></semantics></math> over the
same delays; see Tables <a href="#S7.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 7.4 Mean and variance shifts ‣ 7 The Effect of Delay on ACI Across Residual Regimes ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> and <a href="#S7.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 7.4 Mean and variance shifts ‣ 7 The Effect of Delay on ACI Across Residual Regimes ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>. This is not contradictory because
adaptation duration measures the time required for rolling coverage to return above <math id="S7.SS4.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.89" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.89</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.89</annotation></semantics></math>, not the depth of the coverage failure. The delay-specific
selection of <math id="S7.SS4.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>γ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> may partially offset delayed feedback: the larger step sizes selected at the longest delays permit stronger corrections once feedback becomes available. This may limit adaptation duration even when the initial coverage loss is deeper. The selected step sizes are shown in Figure <a href="#A3.F18" title="Figure 18 ‣ C.3 Mean and Variance Shift ‣ Appendix C Additional Results ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a> in
Appendix <a href="#A3.SS3" title="C.3 Mean and Variance Shift ‣ Appendix C Additional Results ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.3</span></a>.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Shortening the calibration window has different effects across the two families. For mean shifts, <math id="S7.SS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=100</annotation></semantics></math> produces the shorter adaptation duration in <math id="S7.SS4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="24" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>24</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24</annotation></semantics></math> of the <math id="S7.SS4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="28" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>28</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">28</annotation></semantics></math> configurations in Table <a href="#S7.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 7.4 Mean and variance shifts ‣ 7 The Effect of Delay on ACI Across Residual Regimes ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, so the improvement extends across most shift magnitudes and delays. The comparison is particularly informative for <math id="S7.SS4.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau\in\{10,15,20\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau\in\{10,15,20\}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S7.SS4.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=100</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S7.SS4.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=250" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>250</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=250</annotation></semantics></math> select the same <math id="S7.SS4.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>γ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> (Figure <a href="#A3.F18" title="Figure 18 ‣ C.3 Mean and Variance Shift ‣ Appendix C Additional Results ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a>, Appendix <a href="#A3.SS3" title="C.3 Mean and Variance Shift ‣ Appendix C Additional Results ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.3</span></a>). The shorter adaptation durations at these delays can therefore be attributed primarily to faster removal of residuals from the preceding location regime. At <math id="S7.SS4.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau\in\{5,30,40\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>40</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau\in\{5,30,40\}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S7.SS4.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=100</annotation></semantics></math> also improves adaptation duration in most configurations despite selecting a smaller <math id="S7.SS4.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>γ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> than <math id="S7.SS4.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=250" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>250</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=250</annotation></semantics></math>. The results for <math id="S7.SS4.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta=0.5</annotation></semantics></math> are less stable because coverage remains close to the threshold, making adaptation duration sensitive to brief crossings. For variance shifts, the pattern reverses. Table <a href="#S7.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 7.4 Mean and variance shifts ‣ 7 The Effect of Delay on ACI Across Residual Regimes ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> shows that <math id="S7.SS4.p3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=250" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>250</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=250</annotation></semantics></math> produces the
shorter duration in <math id="S7.SS4.p3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="27" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>27</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">27</annotation></semantics></math> of the <math id="S7.SS4.p3.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="35" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>35</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">35</annotation></semantics></math> configurations. Unlike the mean-shift case, <math id="S7.SS4.p3.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=100</annotation></semantics></math> selects a substantially smaller <math id="S7.SS4.p3.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>γ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> at every delay (Figure <a href="#A3.F18" title="Figure 18 ‣ C.3 Mean and Variance Shift ‣ Appendix C Additional Results ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a>, Appendix <a href="#A3.SS3" title="C.3 Mean and Variance Shift ‣ Appendix C Additional Results ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.3</span></a>). The resulting weaker
feedback update likely contributes to the longer coverage dips.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
