<tr id="S7.T5.5.1.7" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S7.T5.5.1.7.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_bb">8</th>
<td id="S7.T5.5.1.7.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb">132</td>
<td id="S7.T5.5.1.7.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="S7.T5.5.1.7.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">103</span></td>

<td id="S7.T5.5.1.7.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb">166</td>

<td id="S7.T5.5.1.7.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb">171</td>

<td id="S7.T5.5.1.7.15" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb">175</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</span></div>
</figure>
<div id="S7.SS4.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS4.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S7.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ 7.4 Mean and variance shifts ‣ 7 The Effect of Delay on ACI Across Residual Regimes ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> shows that larger shifts produce
higher interval scores and greater sensitivity to delay. They also generally
produce higher local coverage errors and favor larger optimal step sizes,
reflecting the need for more aggressive feedback following severe coverage
failures. This pattern is clearest for <math id="S7.SS4.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta=4</annotation></semantics></math> and for the variance ratios
<math id="S7.SS4.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=5</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S7.SS4.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=8</annotation></semantics></math>. Nevertheless, even with larger selected values of
<math id="S7.SS4.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>γ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math>, severe shifts remain more difficult to accommodate than mild
shifts. The corresponding step-size and local-coverage results are reported in
Figures <a href="#A3.F18" title="Figure 18 ‣ C.3 Mean and Variance Shift ‣ Appendix C Additional Results ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a> and
<a href="#A3.F19" title="Figure 19 ‣ C.3 Mean and Variance Shift ‣ Appendix C Additional Results ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">19</span></a> in
Appendix <a href="#A3.SS3" title="C.3 Mean and Variance Shift ‣ Appendix C Additional Results ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.3</span></a>.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS4.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS4.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Shortening the calibration window has a much clearer interval-score benefit for
mean shifts than for variance shifts. For mean shifts, <math id="S7.SS4.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=100</annotation></semantics></math> consistently
produces a noticeably lower score than <math id="S7.SS4.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=250" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>250</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=250</annotation></semantics></math>, in agreement with its generally
shorter adaptation durations. For variance shifts, the reduction in interval
score is comparatively modest, particularly at shorter delays, and occurs
despite generally slower restoration of coverage under <math id="S7.SS4.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=100</annotation></semantics></math>. The two metrics
emphasize different aspects of performance: interval score balances width and
miscoverage over the complete trajectory, whereas adaptation duration measures
local recovery following a transition. The LCE results in
Figure <a href="#A3.F19" title="Figure 19 ‣ C.3 Mean and Variance Shift ‣ Appendix C Additional Results ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">19</span></a> reinforce this distinction. Under
variance shifts, LCE is generally higher for <math id="S7.SS4.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=100</annotation></semantics></math> than for <math id="S7.SS4.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=250" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>250</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=250</annotation></semantics></math>,
consistent with the longer adaptation durations.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<figure id="S7.F9" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2609.07251v1/figures/Delayed_ACI/shift_families__achieved_performance_vs_tau_with_combined_rcal.png" id="S7.F9.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/180;" width="476" height="180" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S7.F9.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 9</span>: </span><span id="S7.F9.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Achieved interval score at the selected step size
<math id="S7.F9.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\star}(\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>γ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma^{\star}(\tau)</annotation></semantics></math> as a function of feedback delay for the mean-shift
family (left) and variance-shift family (right). Colored curves show the
isolated-shift experiments using <math id="S7.F9.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=250" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>250</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=250</annotation></semantics></math>. The solid and dashed black curves show the combined-shift experiments using <math id="S7.F9.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=250" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>250</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=250</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S7.F9.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=100</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively. <math id="S7.F9.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\star}(\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>γ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma^{\star}(\tau)</annotation></semantics></math> is selected separately for each delay,
shift family, calibration-window length, and experiment using the coverage-aware interval-score criterion.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">7.5 </span>Markov-switching — stochastic and recurring regime changes</h3>

<div id="S7.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Using the curve-collapse diagnostic defined in Section <a href="#S6" title="6 Simulated Residual Processes and Diagnostic Framework ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, replacing <math id="S7.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S7.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\mathrm{regime}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>regime</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\mathrm{regime}}</annotation></semantics></math> reduces the within-bin interval-score scatter by approximately <math id="S7.SS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9\%</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S7.SS5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="27\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>27</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">27\%</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S7.SS5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10\%</annotation></semantics></math> under mean, variance, and joint switching, respectively. Although the reduction is modest for mean and joint switching, it is positive for all three families and is strongest under variance switching. The normalization results exhibit substantially stronger alignment: the scatter in the normalized-to-unnormalized interval-score ratio decreases by approximately <math id="S7.SS5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="83\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>83</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">83\%</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S7.SS5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="84\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>84</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">84\%</annotation></semantics></math> for the current-state oracle under variance and joint switching, respectively. We therefore present the main interval-score and normalization results against <math id="S7.SS5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\mathrm{regime}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>regime</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\mathrm{regime}}</annotation></semantics></math>. The corresponding results against the raw delay <math id="S7.SS5.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> are shown in Figures <a href="#A3.F20" title="Figure 20 ‣ C.4 Markov Switching ‣ Appendix C Additional Results ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">20</span></a> and <a href="#A3.F21" title="Figure 21 ‣ C.4 Markov Switching ‣ Appendix C Additional Results ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">21</span></a> in Appendix <a href="#A3.SS4" title="C.4 Markov Switching ‣ Appendix C Additional Results ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.4</span></a>.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S7.F10" title="Figure 10 ‣ 7.5 Markov-switching — stochastic and recurring regime changes ‣ 7 The Effect of Delay on ACI Across Residual Regimes ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> reports the interval score and the mismatch-minus-match score difference for the symmetric chains. Unlike the Gaussian, AR(1), and GARCH(1,1) families, the Markov-switching families were not standardized to unit unconditional variance. Under the symmetric design, <math id="S7.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{0}=\pi_{1}=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{0}=\pi_{1}=0.5</annotation></semantics></math>, and with <math id="S7.SS5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta=4</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S7.SS5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=5</annotation></semantics></math>, the unconditional residual variances are <math id="S7.SS5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S7.SS5.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="13" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>13</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">13</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S7.SS5.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="17" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>17</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">17</annotation></semantics></math> for the mean-, variance-, and joint-switching families, respectively. Their larger absolute interval scores therefore partly reflect greater marginal residual dispersion and are not directly comparable with those of the other residual families. Because <math id="S7.SS5.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{0}=\pi_{1}=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{0}=\pi_{1}=0.5</annotation></semantics></math> for every value of <math id="S7.SS5.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>, the marginal residual distribution is fixed within each Markov-switching family, allowing persistence levels to be compared directly. The top row shows that <math id="S7.SS5.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.99" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.99</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.99</annotation></semantics></math> produces the lowest interval score at the shortest delay but deteriorates rapidly as <math id="S7.SS5.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\mathrm{regime}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>regime</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\mathrm{regime}}</annotation></semantics></math> increases. Under mean switching, the scores for <math id="S7.SS5.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\leq 0.95" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>0.95</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\leq 0.95</annotation></semantics></math> remain nearly constant, whereas the score for <math id="S7.SS5.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.97" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.97</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.97</annotation></semantics></math> is slightly higher and the score for <math id="S7.SS5.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.99" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.99</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.99</annotation></semantics></math> continues to increase. Under variance and joint switching, the configurations with <math id="S7.SS5.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\leq 0.95" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>0.95</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\leq 0.95</annotation></semantics></math> approach similar plateaus before <math id="S7.SS5.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\mathrm{regime}}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>regime</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\mathrm{regime}}=1</annotation></semantics></math>, while <math id="S7.SS5.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.97" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.97</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.97</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S7.SS5.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.99" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.99</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.99</annotation></semantics></math> remain higher.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The mismatch analysis tests whether the deterioration in interval performance is specifically associated with the target falling in a different regime from the one occupied at interval construction. A positive mismatch-minus-match difference therefore indicates an additional interval-score penalty when <math id="S7.SS5.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t}\neq A_{t+\tau}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>≠</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t}\neq A_{t+\tau}</annotation></semantics></math>. This difference is close to zero for the less persistent chains, remains positive for <math id="S7.SS5.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.97" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.97</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.97</annotation></semantics></math>, and is largest for <math id="S7.SS5.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.99" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.99</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.99</annotation></semantics></math>. When switching is frequent (low persistence), the rolling calibration window contains many observations from both regimes and therefore more closely represents their stationary mixture. The resulting intervals are less specific to the regime occupied at the forecast origin, so changing states between the forecast origin and target has relatively little additional effect. Under greater persistence, the calibration window contains fewer regime changes and can become more strongly influenced by the current regime during interval construction. A target generated under the opposite regime is then poorly represented by the recent residual history. This explains both the larger mismatch penalty and the higher interval scores for <math id="S7.SS5.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.97" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.97</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.97</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S7.SS5.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.99" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.99</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.99</annotation></semantics></math> at larger delays.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS5.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS5.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The mismatch penalty is particularly large at the shortest delay for the more persistent chains. At <math id="S7.SS5.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=1</annotation></semantics></math>, a mismatch corresponds to an immediate regime transition, which occurs with probability <math id="S7.SS5.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-p</annotation></semantics></math>; for <math id="S7.SS5.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in\{0.95,0.97,0.99\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0.95</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.97</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.99</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\in\{0.95,0.97,0.99\}</annotation></semantics></math>, these probabilities are only <math id="S7.SS5.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.05</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.05</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S7.SS5.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.03" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.03</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.03</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S7.SS5.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.01" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.01</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.01</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively. Because <math id="S7.SS5.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>γ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> is selected using the average interval score, these rare mismatches have relatively little influence on the selected step size, so intervals can perform well within the current regime while performing poorly immediately after a switch. As <math id="S7.SS5.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> increases, mismatches become more common according to Equation (<a href="#S6.E30" title="In 6.6 Markov-switching — stochastic and recurring regime changes ‣ 6 Simulated Residual Processes and Diagnostic Framework ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">30</span></a>), and the mismatch-minus-match gap generally narrows even as the average interval score can increase.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<figure id="S7.F10" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2609.07251v1/figures/Delayed_ACI/markov_symmetric_interval_score_and_mismatch_gap_vs_rregime_R250.png" id="S7.F10.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/240;" width="476" height="240" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S7.F10.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 10</span>: </span><span id="S7.F10.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Achieved interval score (top) and mismatch-minus-match conditional interval
score (bottom) under symmetric Markov switching with <math id="S7.F10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=250" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>250</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=250</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S7.SS5.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS5.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S7.F11" title="Figure 11 ‣ 7.5 Markov-switching — stochastic and recurring regime changes ‣ 7 The Effect of Delay on ACI Across Residual Regimes ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a> shows a pattern similar to the GARCH results: current-state normalization becomes less effective as <math id="S7.SS5.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\mathrm{regime}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>regime</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\mathrm{regime}}</annotation></semantics></math> increases. The target-state oracle does not exhibit the same deterioration, indicating that the loss in current-state normalization is driven by mismatch between the scale at interval construction and the scale at the target time. Because the target-state oracle uses future state information, it is not deployable; rather, it provides a benchmark for the potential gains from better forecasts of the target-time regime or scale. The normalization gain is smaller under joint switching because normalization addresses the state-dependent variance but not the state-dependent mean.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<figure id="S7.F11" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2609.07251v1/figures/Delayed_ACI/markov_symmetric_normalization_oracles_vs_rregime_R250.png" id="S7.F11.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/185;" width="476" height="185" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S7.F11.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 11</span>: </span><span id="S7.F11.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Normalized-to-unnormalized interval-score ratio for the two oracle
normalization constructions under symmetric Markov switching with <math id="S7.F11.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=250" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>250</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=250</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">7.6 </span>Cross-family comparison of delay-to-memory scaling</h3>

<div id="S7.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We conclude the simulation results by comparing how well the delay-to-memory
reparameterization organizes performance across the persistent residual
families. Table <a href="#S7.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ 7.6 Cross-family comparison of delay-to-memory scaling ‣ 7 The Effect of Delay on ACI Across Residual Regimes ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> reports the reduction in within-bin interval-score scatter obtained by replacing the raw delay <math id="S7.SS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> with the
corresponding delay-to-memory ratio.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>

</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S7.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The strongest collapse occurs for AR(1), where dependence is carried directly
by the residual level. The reduction remains substantial but smaller under
GARCH(1,1), where persistence appears in the conditional variance rather than
the signed residual. For Markov switching, the raw interval score is only
weakly to moderately organized by <math id="S7.SS6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\mathrm{regime}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>regime</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\mathrm{regime}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus, although the
delay-to-memory ratio improves on the raw delay across all three persistent
process classes, the extent of the improvement depends on the form of
non-exchangeability.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The delay-to-memory ratio can be more informative when the outcome of interest is the relative benefit of normalization. Table <a href="#S7.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ 7.6 Cross-family comparison of delay-to-memory scaling ‣ 7 The Effect of Delay on ACI Across Residual Regimes ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> reports the same diagnostic applied to the ratio of normalized to unnormalized interval score. The delay-to-memory ratio reduces scatter by <math id="S7.SS6.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>50</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50\%</annotation></semantics></math> for the GARCH current-scale oracle and by more than <math id="S7.SS6.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="80\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>80</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">80\%</annotation></semantics></math> for the current-state oracle under both variance and joint Markov switching. The contrast between Tables <a href="#S7.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ 7.6 Cross-family comparison of delay-to-memory scaling ‣ 7 The Effect of Delay on ACI Across Residual Regimes ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> and
<a href="#S7.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ 7.6 Cross-family comparison of delay-to-memory scaling ‣ 7 The Effect of Delay on ACI Across Residual Regimes ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> shows that the usefulness of the
delay-to-memory ratio depends on the quantity being examined. Under Markov
switching, <math id="S7.SS6.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\mathrm{regime}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>regime</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\mathrm{regime}}</annotation></semantics></math> provides only a limited collapse of overall
interval performance, but strongly organizes the effect of using
state-dependent scale information. The ratio therefore captures the relevance of state-dependent scale information across the forecast delay more clearly than it characterizes overall performance.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S7.T7" class="ltx_table">

</section>
<section id="S8" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">8 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This paper studies adaptive conformal inference when coverage feedback is delayed by a fixed forecast horizon <math id="S8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>. The phase-wise representation of the delayed recursion yields a long-run coverage bound whose finite-sample deviation depends explicitly on the delay, while the marginal coverage bound provides a complementary characterization by relating coverage deviation to changes in the underlying environment across the forecast horizon and the adaptation rate <math id="S8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>. This motivates asking how the persistence of the residual signal relative to <math id="S8.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> governs finite-sample performance. The simulations investigate this question by introducing a delay-to-memory ratio and testing whether it organizes performance across several mechanistically distinct forms of residual dependence and distributional change.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S8.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p2.1" class="ltx_p">A central finding is that the effect of feedback delay is more informative when interpreted relative to the memory of the residual process than in raw time steps alone. At the same time, the delay-to-memory ratio is not a universal characterization of performance. Its usefulness depends on which feature of the residual distribution carries temporal dependence and on the quantity being evaluated. The relevant memory scale may therefore concern the residual level, its magnitude or variance, or a latent regime. More generally, the ratio is best viewed as a diagnostic of whether information available at prediction time is likely to remain relevant at the forecast target.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S8.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The persistence and shift experiments also expose a limitation of using a single fixed step size throughout an online forecasting sequence. The appropriate <math id="S8.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> depends on both the residual dynamics and the relation between delay and persistence. Under exchangeable residuals, aggressive adaptation reduces efficiency without improving coverage, whereas under settings with informative temporal structure or abrupt distributional change, faster adaptation can be useful. A step size suited to one setting may therefore be too conservative when the distribution changes suddenly and too aggressive once the residual signal becomes weak or uninformative.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S8.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p4.1" class="ltx_p">This motivates coupling delayed ACI with procedures that do not require committing to a single learning rate in advance. Online Expert Aggregation on ACI (AgACI) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zaffran et al., 2022</a>)</cite> and Fully Adaptive Conformal Inference (FACI) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gibbs and Candès, 2024</a>)</cite> use aggregation across candidate learning rates to adapt the step size automatically, providing natural templates for this direction. A complementary direction is to exploit temporal structure more directly. Estimates of residual persistence could help determine how strongly delayed feedback should influence current updates, while dependence across forecast horizons could provide additional information about future errors. Related work has begun to exploit temporal dependence across forecast horizons in online conformal prediction <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang and Hyndman, 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2026</a>)</cite>. A natural question is whether estimates of residual persistence could also be used to determine how strongly delayed feedback should influence the ACI update, while retaining its coverage guarantees. In this broader setting, the delay-to-memory ratio would continue to serve as a diagnostic for when delayed feedback is likely to remain informative.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Proofs for Coverage Guarantees Under Delayed Feedback</h2>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This appendix collects the full derivations supporting the boundedness, long-run coverage, and approximate marginal coverage results for the <math id="A1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>-delayed ACI recursion stated in the main text (Sections <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Boundedness of 𝛼_𝑚^(𝜃) ‣ 4 𝜏-Delayed Adaptive Conformal Inference ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>–<a href="#S4.SS4" title="4.4 Approximate Marginal Coverage ‣ 4 𝜏-Delayed Adaptive Conformal Inference ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>Boundedness of <math id="A1.SS1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}</annotation></semantics></math></h3>

<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each fixed <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>, the phase-wise sequence <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}</annotation></semantics></math> obeys the same Robbins–Monro style update as in standard ACI.
Since <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{m}^{(\theta)}\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>e</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{m}^{(\theta)}\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math>, the change between consecutive updates satisfies</p>
<table id="A1.E31" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E31.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bigl|\alpha_{m+1}^{(\theta)}-\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}\bigr|=\gamma\bigl|\alpha-e_{m}^{(\theta)}\bigr|\leq\gamma." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>e</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bigl|\alpha_{m+1}^{(\theta)}-\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}\bigr|=\gamma\bigl|\alpha-e_{m}^{(\theta)}\bigr|\leq\gamma.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(31)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">From (<a href="#A1.E31" title="In A.1 Boundedness of 𝛼_𝑚^(𝜃) ‣ Appendix A Proofs for Coverage Guarantees Under Delayed Feedback ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">31</span></a>), if <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> then it follows that <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-\gamma\leq\alpha_{m+1}^{(\theta)}\leq 1+\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\gamma\leq\alpha_{m+1}^{(\theta)}\leq 1+\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>. Moreover, the two boundary cases ensure that <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}</annotation></semantics></math> cannot drift further outward:</p>
<ul id="A1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If <math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}&lt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}&lt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}/2&lt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}/2&lt;0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}/2&gt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}/2&gt;1</annotation></semantics></math>, so both thresholds diverge: <math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{Q}_{t_{\theta}(m-1)}(\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}/2)=-\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{Q}_{t_{\theta}(m-1)}(\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}/2)=-\infty</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{Q}_{t_{\theta}(m-1)}(1-\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}/2)=+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{Q}_{t_{\theta}(m-1)}(1-\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}/2)=+\infty</annotation></semantics></math>. The coverage interval is then all of <math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℝ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math>, which forces <math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{m}^{(\theta)}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>e</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{m}^{(\theta)}=0</annotation></semantics></math>. Hence</p>
<table id="A1.Ex20" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{m+1}^{(\theta)}-\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}=\gamma\alpha\geq 0,\quad\Rightarrow\quad\alpha_{m+1}^{(\theta)}\geq\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.889em">,</mo><mo stretchy="false">⇒</mo><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>≥</mo><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{m+1}^{(\theta)}-\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}=\gamma\alpha\geq 0,\quad\Rightarrow\quad\alpha_{m+1}^{(\theta)}\geq\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>

</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}&gt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}&gt;1</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}/2&gt;1-\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}/2&gt;1-\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}/2</annotation></semantics></math>, and monotonicity of <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{Q}_{t_{\theta}(m-1)}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{Q}_{t_{\theta}(m-1)}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{Q}_{t_{\theta}(m-1)}(\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}/2)\geq\hat{Q}_{t_{\theta}(m-1)}(1-\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}/2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{Q}_{t_{\theta}(m-1)}(\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}/2)\geq\hat{Q}_{t_{\theta}(m-1)}(1-\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}/2)</annotation></semantics></math>, so the coverage interval is empty (or a single point). This forces <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{m}^{(\theta)}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>e</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{m}^{(\theta)}=1</annotation></semantics></math>. Hence</p>
<table id="A1.Ex21" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex21.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{m+1}^{(\theta)}-\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}=\gamma(\alpha-1)\leq 0,\quad\Rightarrow\quad\alpha_{m+1}^{(\theta)}\leq\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.889em">,</mo><mo stretchy="false">⇒</mo><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>≤</mo><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{m+1}^{(\theta)}-\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}=\gamma(\alpha-1)\leq 0,\quad\Rightarrow\quad\alpha_{m+1}^{(\theta)}\leq\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Therefore, for all <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math> we have</p>
<table id="A1.Ex22" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex22.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}\in[-\gamma,\,1+\gamma]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn> 1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}\in[-\gamma,\,1+\gamma],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.p3.2" class="ltx_p">exactly as in Lemma 4.1 of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gibbs and Candès (2021)</a></cite>, with the difference being that here <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{m}^{(\theta)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>e</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{m}^{(\theta)}</annotation></semantics></math> is determined by the quantiles <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{Q}_{t_{\theta}(m-1)}(\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}/2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{Q}_{t_{\theta}(m-1)}(\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}/2)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{Q}_{t_{\theta}(m-1)}(1-\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}/2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{Q}_{t_{\theta}(m-1)}(1-\alpha_{m}^{(\theta)}/2)</annotation></semantics></math> fit at time <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{\theta}(m-1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{\theta}(m-1)</annotation></semantics></math> rather than at <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t-1</annotation></semantics></math>, reflecting the <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>-step delay, and it is determined by a two-sided coverage interval rather than a one-sided threshold, reflecting the signed-residual construction.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>Long-Term Coverage Guarantees</h3>

<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We now derive the long-term coverage guarantees for <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>-delayed ACI, following the reasoning of Proposition 4.1 in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gibbs and Candès (2021)</a></cite>. For simplicity, we set <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{0}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{0}=0</annotation></semantics></math> throughout.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Step 1: Phase-wise bound:</h4>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Expanding the recursion in Equation <a href="#S4.E8" title="In 4.1 Alternative Form of 𝜏-DACI ‣ 4 𝜏-Delayed Adaptive Conformal Inference ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> for a fixed phase <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> gives</p>

<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Step 2: Phase sets and notation:</h4>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta\in\{1,\dots,\tau\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta\in\{1,\dots,\tau\}</annotation></semantics></math>, let</p>
<table id="A1.Ex25" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex25.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\theta}\;:=\;\{\,t\in\{1,\dots,T\}:(t-\theta)\bmod\tau=0\,\}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">:=</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi><mo rspace="0.278em" stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\theta}\;:=\;\{\,t\in\{1,\dots,T\}:(t-\theta)\bmod\tau=0\,\}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">be the set of time indices where the <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>-sequence is updated, then <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{\theta}:=|P_{\theta}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{\theta}:=|P_{\theta}|</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of updates in phase <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>. Denote <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{e}^{(\theta)}:=\frac{1}{K_{\theta}}\sum_{m=1}^{K_{\theta}}e^{(\theta)}_{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>e</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub></msubsup><msubsup><mi>e</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{e}^{(\theta)}:=\frac{1}{K_{\theta}}\sum_{m=1}^{K_{\theta}}e^{(\theta)}_{m}</annotation></semantics></math> as the average empirical miscoverage in phase <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>. Therefore, (<a href="#A1.E32" title="In Step 1: Phase-wise bound: ‣ A.2 Long-Term Coverage Guarantees ‣ Appendix A Proofs for Coverage Guarantees Under Delayed Feedback ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">32</span></a>) yields</p>
<table id="A1.Ex26" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex26.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bigl|\bar{e}^{(\theta)}-\alpha\bigr|\;\leq\;\frac{\max\{\alpha^{(\theta)}_{1},\;1-\alpha^{(\theta)}_{1}\}}{\gamma\,K_{\theta}}\;+\;\frac{1}{K_{\theta}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>e</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" rspace="0.280em" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">≤</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn> 1</mn><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0.502em" rspace="0.502em">+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bigl|\bar{e}^{(\theta)}-\alpha\bigr|\;\leq\;\frac{\max\{\alpha^{(\theta)}_{1},\;1-\alpha^{(\theta)}_{1}\}}{\gamma\,K_{\theta}}\;+\;\frac{1}{K_{\theta}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Step 3: From phase-wise to global coverage:</h4>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\texttt{err}_{t}:=\mathbbm{1}\{Y_{t}\notin\hat{\mathcal{C}}^{\tau}_{t}(\alpha_{t})\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">err</mtext><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mn>𝟙</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∉</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mi>τ</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\texttt{err}_{t}:=\mathbbm{1}\{Y_{t}\notin\hat{\mathcal{C}}^{\tau}_{t}(\alpha_{t})\}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the indicator of miscoverage at time t. Partitioning the index set <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{1,\dots,T\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{1,\dots,T\}</annotation></semantics></math> by the phase sets <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> and using the phase timeline <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{\theta}(m)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{\theta}(m)</annotation></semantics></math>, we obtain</p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

P_{\theta}}\texttt{err}_{t_{\theta}(m)}\Biggr)=\sum_{\theta=1}^{\tau}\frac{K_{\theta}}{T}\;\Biggl(\frac{1}{K_{\theta}}\sum_{m=1}^{K_{\theta}}e^{(\theta)}_{m}\Biggr)=\sum_{\theta=1}^{\tau}\frac{K_{\theta}}{T}\bar{e}^{(\theta)}." </table>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The long-term coverage is calculated</p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex28.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left|\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\texttt{err}_{t}-\alpha\right|\leq\sum_{\theta=1}^{\tau}\frac{K_{\theta}}{T}\,\left|\bar{e}^{(\theta)}-\alpha\right|\\
\leq\sum_{\theta=1}^{\tau}\frac{K_{\theta}}{T}\left(\frac{\max\{\alpha^{(\theta)}_{1},\;1-\alpha^{(\theta)}_{1}\}}{\gamma\,K_{\theta}}+\frac{1}{K_{\theta}}\right)\\
" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>T</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">err</mtext><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">≤</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>τ</mi></munderover><mrow><mfrac><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mi>T</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>e</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">≤</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>τ</mi></munderover><mrow><mfrac><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mi>T</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn> 1</mn><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub></mfrac></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\texttt{err}_{t}-\alpha\right|\leq\sum_{\theta=1}^{\tau}\frac{K_{\theta}}{T}\,\left|\bar{e}^{(\theta)}-\alpha\right|\\
\leq\sum_{\theta=1}^{\tau}\frac{K_{\theta}}{T}\left(\frac{\max\{\alpha^{(\theta)}_{1},\;1-\alpha^{(\theta)}_{1}\}}{\gamma\,K_{\theta}}+\frac{1}{K_{\theta}}\right)\\
</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Therefore, the global coverage bound is</p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E33.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left|\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\texttt{err}_{t}-\alpha\right|\;\leq\;\frac{1}{\gamma\,T}\sum_{\theta=1}^{\tau}\max\{\alpha^{(\theta)}_{1},\;1-\alpha^{(\theta)}_{1}\}\;+\;\frac{\tau}{T}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>T</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">err</mtext><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.280em">|</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>τ</mi></munderover><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn> 1</mn><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.502em">+</mo><mfrac><mi>τ</mi><mi>T</mi></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\texttt{err}_{t}-\alpha\right|\;\leq\;\frac{1}{\gamma\,T}\sum_{\theta=1}^{\tau}\max\{\alpha^{(\theta)}_{1},\;1-\alpha^{(\theta)}_{1}\}\;+\;\frac{\tau}{T}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(33)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p3.2" class="ltx_p">In particular, <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\texttt{err}_{t}\to\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>T</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></msubsup><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">err</mtext><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\texttt{err}_{t}\to\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> almost surely as <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>

</section>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.3 </span>Approximate Marginal Coverage</h3>

<div id="A1.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We provide the proof of the <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>-delayed analogue of Theorem 4.2 in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gibbs and Candès (2021)</a></cite>, which bounds the mean-squared deviation of the marginal miscoverage <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M(\alpha_{t}\mid A_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M(\alpha_{t}\mid A_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> from the target <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>.
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Approximate marginal coverage for <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>-Delayed ACI:</span>

Under the setup of Section <a href="#S4.SS4" title="4.4 Approximate Marginal Coverage ‣ 4 𝜏-Delayed Adaptive Conformal Inference ‣ Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a>, assume <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\alpha_{t},A_{t},\texttt{err}_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">err</mtext><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\alpha_{t},A_{t},\texttt{err}_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> is stationary, <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="M(\cdot\mid a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M(\cdot\mid a)</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{Lip}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{Lip}</annotation></semantics></math>-Lipschitz for all <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a\in\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a\in\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math>, and each <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> admits a unique <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha^{*}_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>a</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha^{*}_{a}</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M(\alpha^{*}_{a}\mid a)=\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>a</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M(\alpha^{*}_{a}\mid a)=\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>. Then</p>
<table id="A1.Ex29" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex29.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}\!\left[\bigl(M(\alpha_{t}\mid stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>γ</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mpadded style="width:0.497em;" width="0.497em"><mi>𝔼</mi></mpadded><mo lspace="0em"
